fix(security): close the 2026-09-26 security review findings and their follow-ups (#549)

* fix(portal): a Platform success without a user object is no longer a login

authenticate_customer accepted {"success": true} with no user object as a
valid login whenever its own outgoing HMAC headers looked well-formed, a
branch written to accommodate mock Platform responses. A session created
that way carried user_id=None. The production auth path now maps a login
only when the Platform returns a user object; the four tests that relied
on the lenient branch send a realistic user payload instead, and a new
contract test pins the rejection.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(portal): count failed logins instead of clearing the limiter on every one

The authentication rate limiter decided from the response status. Every
auth view renders 200 on a rejected credential, which the limiter read as
success, so a failed login deleted both the IP and the account counters
and nothing was ever blocked. Views now report the outcome explicitly:
login, MFA code checks and customer switching mark failures, and only a
completed login clears the counters. Password-reset and registration
posts are counted on every request into their own volume bucket, so a
shared office address cannot lock itself out of login by resetting
passwords.

Two latent defects on the same path are fixed with it: the middleware ran
before the messages middleware, so its throttled-browser response would
have raised instead of redirecting, and that redirect pointed at Django's
default /accounts/login/, which the Portal does not serve. The login body
now carries the caller's address for the Platform's own per-client limit.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(platform): give login and reset traffic its own HMAC bucket and a per-client limit

Every Portal request was charged against one fixed-window bucket keyed on
the portal id and the Portal container's own address, so an anonymous
login flood at the Portal could exhaust the bucket and every customer's
API call answered 429. Login, password-reset request and reset
confirmation now charge a separate auth bucket (HMAC_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AUTH_CALLS,
default 120 per window); business traffic keeps the general bucket.

The Portal now forwards the caller's address in the signed login body, and
this commit adds the Platform side of that contract: forwarded_client_ip
reads it only after the middleware verified the signature and never falls
back to the transport address, fixed_window_limited is a reusable
fail-closed counter, and two endpoint throttles key on that address with
their own scopes. The password-reset request endpoint is no longer exempt
from HMAC, so nothing but the Portal can trigger reset mail.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(platform): limit login per caller address and start lockout at the fifth failure

The Portal login endpoint is a plain Django view, so no throttle ever
applied to it and every wrong password cost an Argon2 hash and locked the
account. It now reads the caller address the Portal forwards in the signed
body and refuses the eleventh attempt per minute from one address before
any credential work; requests without a verified forwarded address keep
only the per-portal auth bucket.

Account lockout moves from the first failure to the fifth. The progressive
ladder is indexed from the threshold, so the fifth failure locks for five
minutes rather than the two hours the old index would have produced. The
lockout tests that were written for a threshold of one are pinned to it,
and a new test covers the ladder at the shipping default.

Password-reset request and confirmation require a signed Portal call and
carry the per-portal throttles plus a per-caller reset limit.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(api): enforce customer roles on billing, order, payment and ticket endpoints

Membership validation fetched the CustomerMembership row and discarded its
role, so a read-only viewer could list and download invoices and proformas,
create and confirm orders, create payment intents, rewrite the billing
address, toggle auto-renew and open tickets. A new require_customer_role_in
decorator replaces require_customer_authentication on those endpoints:
billing data, orders and payments need the owner or billing role, ticket
writes need owner, billing or tech. A wrong role gets the same uniform 403
as a missing membership so the response does not reveal roles, the
session-validation shortcut never applies when roles are required, and the
membership's user is recorded as a ticket's creator.

The Portal mirrors the matrix on its own views as defence in depth and
renders a small denial partial for HTMX targets instead of plain text. The
denial helper on the payment endpoints copied the unrendered DRF response's
text/html content type over its JSON body; it now keeps application/json.
An unused client method that could never have worked is removed.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(auth): bind Portal sessions to the password and fail closed on rejection

A password change never reached the customer's other Portal sessions. The
Platform's cleanup scanned its own session table for Django's auth key,
which no Portal session carries, and Portal validation only checked that
the user was active. Worse, a Platform 401 on session validation surfaced
in the Portal as a generic API error, which the middleware treated as an
outage and failed open, so even a disabled account kept access.

Login now returns Django's session auth hash, the Portal stores it apart
from profile data and sends it on every validation, and the Platform
rejects a stale hash, accepting secret-key fallback hashes and echoing the
current one so the Portal upgrades. Any password change or reset therefore
revokes older sessions at their next validation. The Portal treats a 401
or 403 from validation as an authoritative denial, flushes the session,
and no longer defers a denial inside the soft-grace window; transport
errors and 5xx keep the bounded fail-open of ADR-0017, which gains an
addendum. The Platform password-change endpoint still revokes the user's
own Platform sessions and records an accurate security event.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(billing): grant reverse charge only on VIES evidence for the invoiced VAT number

The reverse-charge decision zero-rated an EU business whenever it had a
company name, any VAT number string and the VAT-payer flag, all of which
the customer controlled through the Portal, and the customer endpoint even
wrote the eligibility flag the VIES task was meant to own. The VIES result
was never consulted: it wrote a flag the standard branch never read, it
only ran for four country prefixes, a changed number kept the old
number's status, a slow validation could persist one number's result onto
another, and an outage during the nightly sweep downgraded valid
customers. A second, profile-blind decision lived in the amount
calculator.

One pure function now decides evidence: VIES status valid and the exact
normalised VAT number matching the one being invoiced. Every document
context derives it, the resolver requires it behind a policy setting that
defaults to on, and the legacy amount calculator delegates to the resolver
without an audit write. VAT-number changes clear prior evidence before
validation is queued, validation re-reads the profile under lock and
discards results for a changed number, a VIES outage keeps evidence
verified within the grace window, and neither the customer endpoint nor
the staff form can set the derived flag. A data migration clears legacy
human-set flags; a command backfills validation and reports unpaid
zero-tax orders that now fail preflight with an explicit message.
ADR-0049 records the decision and its relation to ADR-0047.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(deps): move to Django 5.2.17 and urllib3 2.8.0 and cap Portal request bodies

The lockfile pinned Django 5.2.12 and urllib3 2.6.3, both superseded by
releases that close published advisories, while pyproject already
admitted the newer versions. The Portal reverse proxy accepted request
bodies of any size, so an oversized upload reached Django before the
application's 1 MiB attachment limit could reject it.

Upgrade both packages in uv.lock without touching constraints, add a
lock-upgrade Makefile target so future bumps go through one documented
command that also re-syncs the venv, and cap request bodies at 5MB on
the Portal handle of both shipped Caddyfiles. Both files validate with
the official Caddy image.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(portal): keep the method check ahead of the billing role guard on order views

A GET on the POST-only order endpoints answered 403 for a session
without a resolved role, because the role guard ran before the method
check. The method check is identity-independent, so it now runs first
and a GET is refused with 405 for every caller.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(tickets): scope related services to the customer and turn service action requests into tickets

A customer could attach any service to a ticket by ID because the create
serializer exposed the foreign key unfiltered, and the detail serializer
echoed whatever the row pointed at. The field is now a primary-key field
whose queryset is narrowed to the authenticated customer, so a foreign ID
and a nonexistent one produce the same validation error, the detail view
returns the service only when it belongs to the ticket's customer, and a
data migration detaches the legacy links that cross customers.

The Portal posted service upgrade, downgrade, suspend and cancel requests
to a route the Platform never registered, and omitted the user from the
signed body. The route now exists and opens a support ticket in a
"Service Requests" category through a creation helper shared with the
ticket endpoint; suspend and cancel need the owner or billing role and a
reason, other actions need owner, billing or tech, and the ticket-opened
audit event carries the requesting user. The Portal passes the user,
guards the view with the support-role check and links the new ticket.

The refund-request views in orders and billing created their category with
defaults naming SLA fields the model does not have, a latent 500 whenever
the category row was absent. The defaults are removed.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(users): make Portal password reset work end to end

The Portal's reset page logged the request and never called the
Platform, and the Platform endpoint rendered email templates that did not
exist, so every request failed with a 500 before a customer could get a
link. Token and password-policy failures were raised inside save() and
also surfaced as 500s, and the Platform had no notion of the Portal's
public address to put in a link.

A new portal.public_base_url setting supplies the address; an unset or
malformed value is an ImproperlyConfigured error and stays a 500, while
token and policy failures now run in validate() and return 400 with field
errors. The email templates exist, and a completed reset clears the
account lockout so a locked-out customer can recover. The Portal calls
the request endpoint, adds a confirm view and form behind the existing
public /password-reset/ prefix, forwards the client address on both calls
so the per-client reset limit keys, and marks a rejected token as an
authentication failure for the Portal limiter.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(auth): make the login limiters hold up in production topologies

An independent review of the throttle work found three ways it would not
behave in production. Every shipped topology leaves the Portal's trusted
proxy list empty, so every client resolves to the reverse proxy's address
and each per-IP budget, Portal and Platform alike, becomes one shared
bucket: a denial-of-service switch. The Platform's fixed windows keyed a
counter whose expiry the database cache reset on every increment, so a
busy bucket never reopened. And the Portal client returned None for a 5xx
or transport failure, which the login view reported as a wrong password
and charged to the brute-force counters.

The Portal now reads PORTAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS into its trusted proxy
list, production and staging refuse to start without it, the deployment
check becomes an error outside DEBUG, and every compose file, Ansible
template and env example forwards the variable. When clients cannot be
told apart the IP and volume budgets stand down with one logged warning,
the account budget stays, and the client omits the address from every
signed body so the Platform's per-client limits opt out too. Both
Platform limiters key counters by window index, so a window's identity
no longer depends on backend TTLs; a peek before authentication and a
charge only on rejection mean successful logins never consume the
per-client budget. The client re-raises throttles, transport failures and
5xx responses so the view shows the unavailable message without marking
a failure. MFA re-authentication failures use a per-user budget instead
of the pre-login IP bucket, and a denied customer switch no longer counts
as a credential guess.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* docs: record the security review fixes and the new operator prerequisites

CHANGELOG gains the Security, Fixed and Added entries for the 2026-09-26
review, and the pre-deployment checklist lists the Portal trusted-proxy
variable, the portal URL setting and the VIES backfill command that the
fixes require before customer traffic.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(auth): end a session only on the Platform's explicit rejection and bind VAT evidence to the country

Independent reviews of the role, session-binding and VAT-evidence work
found two regressions and several smaller gaps.

The Portal treated any 401 or 403 from session validation as a stale
credential and flushed the session. Two other layers emit those codes:
the inter-service HMAC check and the portal-authentication guard, both of
which fail during a secret rotation or a mixed-secret rolling deploy, so
a configuration fault would have signed every customer out while the
service was otherwise healthy. Only a body carrying the Platform's
explicit `active: false` now ends the session; every other error stays
on the bounded fail-open path ADR-0017 defines. A session whose stored
hash is empty is validated immediately instead of being trusted for a
revalidation interval, and the user-info endpoint returns the signed
caller instead of whichever member the database returned first. Viewer
and tech members no longer receive the tax and billing profiles in the
customer detail payload, the Portal tax-profile page needs the billing
role, and the plain authentication decorator now carries the same
introspection marker as the role decorator so both stacking orders are
caught by the signature guard.

The new VAT-number format check rejected every non-EU number, and the
Portal re-posts the stored value on every submit, so a customer holding a
British or Swiss number could no longer change any field of their tax
profile. Both write paths now validate through one helper that applies
the EU format rule only to EU-issued numbers, resolved against the
billing country. Reverse-charge evidence additionally requires the VAT
number to be issued by the billing-address country, so a business cannot
zero-rate itself by moving only its address, and the evidence
normalisation matches the revalidation sweep so accepted evidence can
always be refreshed. The outage grace no longer rejects a verification
timestamp a few seconds in the future, the stale allowlist entry for the
derived eligibility flag is gone, and the preflight message names missing
evidence only when that is the cause.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(billing): resolve a VAT number against the billing country when queueing VIES

Accepting unprefixed and legacy Greek VAT numbers left the VIES pipeline
assuming Romania. An unprefixed German number was queued and checked as
a Romanian one and rejected on format, and a GR-prefixed number was never
queued because the EU list spells Greece EL, so those customers could not
earn the evidence reverse charge now requires and stayed on destination
VAT. The signal and the validation task resolve the number against the
customer's billing country through one helper, with GR and EL treated as
the same issuer.

The blocked-orders report treated any valid profile as evidence; it now
applies the resolver's own conditions, a VAT payer whose verified number
is the invoiced one and was issued by the billing country, so it lists
exactly the orders preflight blocks. The Portal reset form promised eight
characters where the Platform requires twelve; it now enforces and states
twelve before the round trip.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* feat(common): add an atomic fixed-window counter and claim store to both services

Every counter in both services used the cache's add-then-incr shape.
Under the database cache that increment is a read followed by a write
with no timeout, so concurrent hits lose updates and the caller's window
is replaced by the backend default; the in-memory cache the Portal runs
in production keeps each gunicorn worker's counters, idempotency claims
and nonce replay guards to itself.

The new store keeps one row per key in the service database and
increments it with a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING
statement, which is atomic per row on SQLite and PostgreSQL and returns
the operation's own count. Windows start at the first hit and expire on
their own clock. Claims reuse the same statement: a claim is acquired when
the returned count is one, can be completed with a result, looked up by
another worker, and released only by its owner. Both copies of the module
and of its test suite are byte-identical, enforced by the cross-service
parity test, which now runs under the integration target.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(api): remove the HMAC bypass and the unsigned registration duplicate, uniform 403 bodies

A DEBUG-gated bypass in the payment endpoints' authentication helper
returned the customer without any role check whenever the flag was set,
so twenty-three tests exercised those endpoints without a signature and
without the billing role they now require. The flag, its settings and
its dedicated tests are gone; the endpoint tests sign their requests as
an owner.

The Platform exposed two registration endpoints: the signed one the
Portal calls and an HMAC-exempt duplicate with a looser throttle that
nothing called. The duplicate and its exemption are removed.

Five sibling guards still named the required role in their 403 bodies
and carried none of the no-store headers the uniform denial adds; they
now return the same body as every other denial. The Portal's single-flight
validation lock is acquired atomically per session under a process lock,
released only by its owner, and a throttled revalidation counts toward
the fail-open breaker instead of raising. The test layout audit's
suspicious-name regex now matches whole tokens, so "fixed" and "rounding"
no longer trip it, with its own tests.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(billing): default the VAT report period to the local calendar date

The report's default period ended on the UTC date while its invoice filter
evaluates created_at in the configured time zone, so between midnight and
three in Bucharest the day's invoices vanished from the screen, and the
screen tests failed whenever the suite ran in that window. Both defaults now
come from the local date, and a frozen-clock test pins the evening case.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(users): index sessions per user in the session store and revoke by index

Revoking a user's other sessions decoded every row of the session table
on each password or two-factor change. A session store subclass now
records the session key against the authenticated user on every save and
removes it on delete, which covers login through both branches of
Django's login(), every cycle_key() including update_session_auth_hash,
and sessions created outside login(). A data migration backfills the
index once from the existing rows, a scheduled reconcile indexes any
session an old worker created during a rolling deploy, and the two
revocation helpers delete exactly the indexed keys. An empty index for a
user who demonstrably holds a session is logged as an alarm rather than
reported as success.
The index references the user without a database constraint: Django keeps
the session row of a hard-deleted user and re-saves it on every later
request, so a constrained reference would turn that browser's login
redirect into a server error.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(common): move the Platform counters to the shared store

Seven Platform sites counted through the cache's add-then-incr shape: the
login and HMAC fixed windows, the view rate-limit decorator, the ANAF
quota tracker, the registrar circuit breaker, the welcome-invite guard
and the email rate limiter. Under the database cache those increments
lost concurrent updates and replaced each caller's window with the
backend default, and the Redis rate-limit alias they were meant to use
was configured but never read.

Every site now calls the counter store for its whole lifecycle: check,
increment, release and reset. Request budgets reserve before deciding,
so concurrent requests at the limit admit exactly the budget; the email
service reserves before delivery so an exhausted or unavailable store
cannot send uncounted mail; the invite guard and the breaker keep the
first hit's expiry. Each limiter keeps its own fail-closed arm, and the
kill switch still leaves the store untouched. The unused rate-limit
cache alias and its settings are removed. A concurrency test drives
eight connections through the login window and checks the exact count,
and the breaker tests exercise real gateway calls instead of the cache
mock.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(deploy): serve the Platform on its own hostname behind an allowlist and route webhooks correctly

The single-domain Caddy configuration split one hostname by path between
two services that both own /dashboard/, /billing/, /tickets/ and /api/:
the customer dashboard was routed to the Platform, Platform webhooks fell
through to the Portal, and both health handles pointed at routes that do
not exist. The two-domain Ansible templates served the whole Platform
publicly by default, with their health exemption placed only in the
unrestricted branch.

Every configuration now gives each service its own hostname. On the
Platform hostname the health endpoint, the webhook receivers and the API
are reachable first as sibling handles; everything else requires the
client address to be in PLATFORM_ALLOWED_CIDRS, which defaults to loopback
so a fresh deployment refuses remote staff access until the operator sets
it. The compose files and the Ansible Docker template forward both
hostnames to both Django services, the Ansible defaults follow the same
loopback rule, and the value is documented as space-separated because a
comma stops Caddy at parse time.

A deploy test suite renders the templates and parses the static files to
check route ownership and the examples, and, where a Docker daemon is
reachable, validates every configuration with the official image, proves
a comma-separated allowlist fails validation, and drives requests through
a live Caddy container to show that forwarded-for headers from an
untrusted peer do not open the staff gate. The suite runs under the
integration target.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(billing): require fresh, referenced and name-matched VIES evidence before reverse charge

Reverse charge was granted on a valid VIES status and an exact number
alone. The verification timestamp was written but never consulted, the
consultation reference was carried forward from an earlier response
when a new one lacked it, the verified company name was never compared
with the invoiced name, a staff zero-rate override bypassed the
evidence gate for EU cross-border businesses, and the sweep only
re-queued profiles that still had a cache row.

Evidence now has to be at most billing.vies_evidence_max_age_days old,
carry the consultation reference of the response that produced it, and
name a legal entity whose distinctive tokens appear in the invoiced
identity, each behind its own setting. A valid response without a
reference is stored as format-only. Every refusal is logged and written
as an audit event that the staff tax page lists, at most once per hour
for an identical refusal. New evidence snapshots are version 2 and
freeze the lifetime they were judged by, so the D390 report judges age
from the snapshot rather than the cache's recheck date; version-1
documents keep their historical treatment. A zero override for an EU
cross-border VAT payer is refused without evidence unless the profile
states an exemption reason, which the staff forms now require, and the
resolver reports the decision in its reasoning. The sweep and the
validation command select valid profiles missing a timestamp, a
reference or a cache row in SQL, and the command's blocked-orders report
lists name mismatches and incomplete profiles so operators can remediate
before the gates take effect. The staff forms also accept VAT numbers
from other member states, which they rejected before.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(users): bind sessions to a monotonic MFA credential version

Enabling or disabling MFA left every existing session valid, because
the session binding hashed the password alone and the MFA fields cannot
be hashed: the backup codes change on ordinary use, and hashing the
enabled flag would revive a revoked session after off, on, off.

Each user gets a credential version in its own row, bumped under a row
lock inside the same transaction as every MFA state change: enrolment,
disable, disable-all and recovery cleanup, including the staff web
disable view, which used to clear the fields directly. Untouched
accounts keep today's hash, so no deployment signs anyone out; a bump
only ever grows, so no earlier hash becomes valid again. The MFA API
returns the new binding so the Portal can store it before rotating its
session, the Portal treats a false success body as a failure, an
eight-digit code can no longer complete enrolment, and the staff
enrolment view keeps the secret the user verified instead of generating
a fresh one.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(portal): move the Portal counters and claims to the shared store and gate startup on its table

Every Portal counter lived in the in-memory cache of one gunicorn worker:
the login, re-authentication and volume budgets, the API and cart
limiters, the fail-open breaker, the checkout idempotency guard, the
payment confirmation guard and the webhook and nonce replay guards.
Concurrent requests on different workers could each pass, a completed
checkout could not be replayed once the cart was cleared, and a lost
claim could be released by a request that never held it.

Every site now uses the shared counter store. Request budgets reserve
before deciding, so concurrent requests at the limit admit exactly the
budget; failure budgets record after the outcome; a store failure
denies. Checkout claims carry a token, publish the Platform order id on
success so a retry on any worker replays the confirmation, and are
released only by their owner on failure; the webhook and nonce guards
use the same claims. The Portal database now holds the counter table
next to sessions: the entrypoint, the native systemd unit and the
Ansible role run the two scoped migrations and the deployment checks
before serving, a deploy-time system check refuses to start without the
table, the entrypoint deletes a database only after an integrity check
proves it corrupt, and the native health gate probes a route the limiter
covers. ADR-0050 records that the Portal database may hold
infrastructure tables and never business data. Portal tests that now
touch the store run as database test cases.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* feat(common): add a bounded sweep for expired counters to both services

The store culls one batch of expired rows at random on writes, which
keeps a busy table small but leaves expired rows behind once a table
goes quiet. Both services gain a cull_counters command that deletes rows
past the grace period in bounded batches; the Portal runs it at container
start next to clearsessions and nightly from the native role's cron, and
the Platform registers a daily task next to the system status check. The
parity test covers the command.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(common): close the review findings on the counter store, its call sites and the Caddy routes

The Platform now refuses a deployment whose counter table is missing, as
the Portal already did, instead of booting and denying every limited
request. The email provider bounce webhooks and the recipient
unsubscribe page are public on the Platform hostname; the staff
allowlist had put them behind the gate. The cull grace drops from an
hour to a minute, because an expired row is invisible to every read and
short-window keys were pinning the table for an hour per address. A
duplicate checkout from a browser gets a notice and a redirect rather
than raw JSON, a store error while clearing the fail-open counter no
longer ends a validated session, a failed email delivery gives its
reservation back so an outage cannot burn the budget, and the
post-dispatch denial keeps the uniform response timing.

The registrar contract tests move to database test cases now that the
breaker reads the store, the three infrastructure models join the audit
model allowlist, and the ANAF quota tracker rejects a negative increment
explicitly instead of failing on the store's check constraint. ADR-0050
records the per-request write cost on SQLite and that failure budgets
are bounded by the limit plus the concurrency, never extra successes.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(billing): close the review findings on the VIES evidence gate

The audit write that records a refusal can no longer fail a VAT
calculation; the decision stands and the failure is logged. The name
rule treats "&", "and" and their equivalents as connectors, drops tokens
shorter than three characters so spaced abbreviations cannot count as
identity, and knows the legal forms of the remaining member states, so
"A & B Consulting SRL" matches "A and B Consulting SRL" and "Acme S. R.
L." matches "ACME SRL". A valid VIES answer without a consultation
reference downgrades the status but keeps the earlier referenced proof
on record instead of erasing it, and the sweep re-checks incomplete
profiles two hundred at a time so the first run after deploy cannot
send the whole customer base to a throttled VIES at once. The D390
report treats an absent proof snapshot as the historical "not recorded"
shape whatever the evidence version. The blocked-orders report uses the
pure decision, so running it records nothing, and also lists zero-rate
overrides that now need an exemption reason. The staff "name differs"
warning follows the policy setting, and the order preview test carries
the evidence fields the gate now requires.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* fix(users): close the review findings on the session index and the MFA binding

Adding or removing a WebAuthn credential now rotates the credential
version like every other MFA state change, so the sessions that
accepted the old set of factors are revoked. Clearing expired sessions
removes their index rows in the same transaction, so the index can no
longer outlive the sessions it mirrors. The reconcile walks only live,
unindexed sessions, in key order and without row locks, and resolves
users once per batch instead of once per row. The Portal keeps its
current session binding when a Platform response omits the new one,
which an old worker does during a rolling deploy; writing an empty
binding there signed the user out on the next request. The migration
that adds the credential version states the deploy order, the
revocation helper states why an unindexed session is inert, the layout
audit also flags the plural forms of its bare tokens, and the Portal
middleware docstring describes the per-session lease.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* docs: record the second round of security review fixes

The changelog lists the new settings, commands and deployment variables,
the fixes to the VAT report period, the Portal validation lease, the staff
VAT forms, staff MFA enrolment and the layout audit, and the six security
changes: session revocation on MFA change, the session index, the shared
counter store, the two-hostname Caddy configuration with the staff
allowlist, the hardened VIES evidence rules and the removal of the test
bypass and the unauthenticated registration duplicate.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

* test(integration): admit the counter store in the Portal isolation check

The cross-service isolation test required every Portal models module to be
empty. ADR-0050 lets the Portal database hold sessions and the counter store,
so the check now allows exactly the Counter re-export in the common app and
still refuses any other model on the Portal side.

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Claudiu Ciungan <claudiu@captainpragmatic.com>

commit.message:
feat(settings-engine): Wave 1-3 — super_admin role + read/write API + test actions

Lets non-technical school admins self-serve operational config (SMTP, S3,
OIDC, Anthropic API key, etc.) that previously required editing .env and
restarting. Demo-to-pilot conversion becomes point-and-click instead of
shell-and-engineer.

WAVE 1 — foundation
─────────────────────
- Migration 000057 settings table (scope/key/value_plain/value_encrypted/
  value_type + 4 CHECK constraints + UNIQUE(scope, scope_id, key))
- Migration 000058 widens users.role CHECK to include 'super_admin'
- Setting GORM model with BeforeCreate defaults
- settings.Service with Get/GetEffective/Set/Clear; resolution order:
  user → account-parent-chain → instance → env → default. Secrets pass
  through auth.secretbox before storage; audit_log fires on every
  set/clear with no value in payload (incl. for non-secrets)
- 22-entry catalog covers SMTP/S3/Anthropic/SAML/OIDC/passkeys/branding/
  quotas. JWT_SECRET, MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, DATABASE_URL, ENVIRONMENT,
  FRONTEND_URL deliberately excluded (chicken-and-egg with the store
  that holds them).
- RequireSuperAdmin middleware + Protected/JWT path special-cases the
  role for cross-tenant access. Setup wizard promotes the first user to
  super_admin (was 'admin').

WAVE 2 — read API + Canvas-CVE-class hardening
────────────────────────────────────────────────
- GET /api/v1/superadmin/settings (list, secrets masked)
- GET /api/v1/superadmin/settings/:key (single, secrets masked)
- GET /api/v1/superadmin/settings/groups (catalog vocabulary, no live
  values — separate response shape so a UI bug can't unmask via
  debug serialization)
- Mounted via registerSuperAdminRoutes — the ONLY authorized place to
  attach /superadmin/* routes, structural protection against forgetting
  RequireSuperAdmin on a new endpoint
- Wave 2 audit (Canvas-LMS site_admin CVE precedent):
  - M3: dropped JWT-claim-derived is_super_admin Locals. Demoted
    super_admin used to retain cross-tenant powers via assertSameTenant
    for up to 24h (JWT TTL). Only DB-rechecking writers may now set
    the Locals; regression test in middleware/auth_test.go.
  - M1: setup wizard now wraps CompleteSetup in pg_advisory_lock to
    serialize across pods. Previously a 3-pod deployment hit
    concurrently could mint three super_admins.

WAVE 3 — write API + test actions + SSRF defense
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- PUT/DELETE /api/v1/superadmin/settings/:key — write/clear with
  account-existence validation
- POST /api/v1/superadmin/settings/test/{email,oidc,anthropic,s3} —
  exercise current effective config against external dependencies
  for fast operator feedback
- Per-action rate limit (1/30s per (super_admin, action)) — distinct
  test endpoints don't share buckets, so operators can chain
  email→oidc→anthropic without delay but can't loop-test
- Threat model: super_admin authority is the deployment's settings,
  NOT its network position. Each test action explicitly bounded:
  - email: sends to caller's own email only (not body-controlled);
    no open-relay vector
  - oidc: SSRF guard (https-only, port 443, public-unicast IPs only,
    7 blocked hostname suffixes incl. .internal/.local, no redirects
    via CheckRedirect=http.ErrUseLastResponse)
  - anthropic: endpoint is a const (api.anthropic.com hard-coded);
    no body param can redirect the API key; also refuses redirects
  - s3: object key is paper-lms-settings-test/<crypto-rand-hex>.txt;
    body params named "key"/"object"/"path" are ignored
- Wave 3 audit fixes (post-shipping checklist):
  - C1 CRITICAL: OIDC discovery test followed 3xx redirects without
    re-running validateExternalURL — attacker.com → 302 → 169.254.169.254
    bypassed the SSRF guard entirely. Fixed with CheckRedirect override
    on both OIDC and Anthropic clients.
  - H2 HIGH: Clear handler defaulted to scope=instance on missing
    body. Destructive endpoint → now requires explicit scope (400).
  - M3/M4: test-action audit row now carries IP, User-Agent, and
    admin_account_id (or account_id) for forensic filterability.

TEST COVERAGE
─────────────
- 24 settings.Service unit cases (resolution chain at every scope
  combination, secret encrypt/decrypt round-trip, audit emission,
  cycle-safe parent walk)
- 13 super_admin role-gate cases including Canvas-CVE-class regressions
  (root-account admin must NOT inherit super-admin; near-miss role
  strings like "Super_Admin" must reject)
- 10 read-API handler cases (masking, source resolution, vocabulary
  shape, parent-chain hint, garbage input handling)
- 26 write-API + test-action cases (account-existence guard, scope
  validation, secret-not-in-response, audit emission, no-open-relay
  for email, SSRF rejection for OIDC, no-body-override for Anthropic
  endpoint, no-body-override for S3 key)
- 40+ SSRF guard table cases (loopback/RFC1918/link-local/cloud-
  metadata/CGNAT/IETF-doc/IPv6 ULA/internal suffixes)
- M3 regression test locks "JWT-claim does not set is_super_admin
  Locals" — failure mode that would re-introduce the cross-tenant
  bypass

OUT OF SCOPE (next waves)
──────────────────────────
- Wave 4: React frontend panel at /superadmin/settings
- Wave 5: refactor env-var consumers (SMTPSender, S3StorageBackend,
  AIAssistService, OIDCHandler, PasskeyEngine, SAMLHandler) to read
  through the settings service
- TOCTOU DNS-rebinding hardening on validateExternalURL (defense-in-
  depth; super-admin-only attacker model makes this acceptable for v1)

Migrations apply clean from a fresh DB. AUTO_MIGRATE registration
updated; CI parity test will validate on next push.

Docs: docs/super-admin.md (operator-facing) + extensive header comments
in handlers/super_admin_settings.go and handlers/super_admin_settings_write.go
laying out the threat model and security contract.

commit.message:
feat: requester role with admin approval (stacks on #2662) (#2670)

* feat(auth): add the requester role and keep it through OIDC group sync

Role names become constants in internal/auth (RoleAdmin, RoleUser,
RoleRequester) with one ValidRole check. The six places that validate a
role call it: GetOrCreateByOIDC, SetRole and SetRoleUnguarded in
internal/db, normalizeOIDCRole in internal/config, and
WithOIDCDefaultRole and resolveProvisionRole in the OIDC handler.
BINDERY_OIDC_DEFAULT_ROLE=requester is now a supported value. The user
management API creates a requester when asked.

The last admin guard in SetRole checked role == "user", so demoting the
last admin to requester would have gone through. It now refuses any
role that is not admin.

OIDC group sync set "user" for every login outside the admin group,
which would turn a requester into a full user at each sign in. The rule
is now: in the admin group gives admin; outside it, an admin gets the
configured default role (user when that default is admin, so leaving
the group always demotes); anyone else keeps their role.

Nothing routes on the new role yet. The API guard follows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* feat(auth): hold requesters to an allow list on every API route

auth.RestrictRequester sits in useAPIAuth right after auth.Middleware,
so it covers both the /api/v1 tree and the Arr compatible /api tree. For
a requester it matches the method and path against RequesterAllowList
with a chi router built once at startup, and answers 403 for anything
else. The router in main() cannot be enumerated in a test, so the list
is an allow list: a route added later is closed to requesters until
someone lists it.

The list is health, the session routes, the three metadata searches the
Add dialog uses, the image proxy, and the requester's own /requests
routes (added with the requests API). Admin and user requests pass
untouched, as do requests the auth mode admits as the install. A signed
in user whose role cannot be read is restricted, so a lookup failure
fails closed.

Matching refuses any path that could route differently from its plain
reading: a set RawPath (encoded slash, escaped letter), anything
path.Clean would change (dot segments, doubled or trailing slash), and a
leftover percent sign, backslash or control character. HEAD matches as
GET. Method override headers are never read, and a chi routing method
that disagrees with r.Method is refused.

The three search routes go through a per user token bucket (20 burst,
one every 3 seconds) held in a map bounded at 1024 users with idle
eviction, because each call spends metadata provider quota.

OPDS serves book files, so OPDSAuth now refuses requesters on both the
cookie and the Basic credential paths.

The BINDERY_URL_BASE mount moves out of main() into mountUnderURLBase,
unchanged, so the route tests can put the real prefix handling in front
of the auth stack.

Tests: 81 denied routes, each in HEAD, trailing slash, doubled slash,
dot segment, mixed case, encoded slash and escaped letter spellings;
every allow list entry passes; FuzzRequesterAllowList over raw request
lines; chi.Walk over every register* helper; both trees with and without
a URL base through the real provider; OPDS by cookie and by Basic;
demotion applies on the next request; the limiter bound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* feat(api): let requesters ask for books and authors, and admins approve

Migration 089 adds the requests table (one row per owner, kind and
foreign id; owner cascades on user delete; decided_by and the result ids
go NULL when their rows go) and notifications.on_request_created, off
for every existing notification.

POST /requests takes exactly kind, foreignId and mediaType, from a body
capped at 4 KiB, and refuses any other field. The server looks the item
up at the metadata provider and stores the title and author it reports,
cleaned and capped, plus a payload it builds itself. It answers 409 with
a sentence when the item is already in the library or this user already
asked, and 429 past requests.max_pending_per_user (default 25, a new
setting). GET /requests lists the caller's own requests with fulfilment
derived at list time: a join to the book's status, and one grouped query
per page for an author's import progress. DELETE /requests/{id}
withdraws the caller's own pending request. Every owner query filters on
owner_user_id whether tenancy is on or not.

GET /requests/library is the requester's read only browse: a projection
selected column by column (id, title, author, primary series, cover,
status, formats present) and copied field by field into its own type.
It never reads a file path. A reflection test pins the response type to
that field list.

The admin routes sit behind RequireAdmin: the queue, a pending count
for the nav badge, approve and decline. Approve claims the row with a
compare and swap on status, so of two admins approving at once exactly
one add runs and the other gets 409; a claim older than five minutes is
treated as abandoned. It revalidates the stored payload against the row,
rechecks the library, and runs addBookCore or createAuthorCore through a
narrow requestAdder interface that *AuthorHandler satisfies, in a
context carrying the requester's id so the new rows are theirs. The
admin supplies the profiles, root folder, monitor options, format and
search on add. Any failure releases the claim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* test(api): keep the catalogue sync when an approval searches on add

The base branch now refuses SearchOnAdd together with SkipCatalogueSync
in createAuthorCore, because the search only runs inside that sync.
Approval never skips the sync; the params say so explicitly, a test runs
an author approval with search on add through the real core and checks
the params the fake records, and the sentinel, should a later change
reach it, maps to a sentence an admin can act on and releases the claim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* feat(notifier): send requestCreated when a requester asks for something

The notifier recipe, followed as it stands: the EventRequestCreated
constant, a normalizeEventPayload case ("Book Requested" or "Author
Requested", the title, the author and who asked), a matchesEvent case,
Notification.OnRequestCreated, the on_request_created column in the
four notification statements, and a Request toggle and badge in the
notifications settings. The column from migration 089 defaults to 0, so
nothing fires until an admin turns it on.

The requests handler sends the event after a request is stored, without
holding up the requester's response. The payload text comes from a
publicly editable provider and a self chosen username and lands in a
chat channel, so title, author and username have control and invisible
characters stripped, are capped, and have every at sign replaced with
the fullwidth at sign so they cannot mention a channel (security review
item S3). A refused request sends nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* feat(web): give requesters their own shell and admins a request queue

AuthContext exposes role and isRequester, plus useIsRequester for
components that also render outside the provider. The nav is picked by
role. A requester gets three pages and nothing else: Library (the read
only projection, with search and no links into book pages), Request (the
metadata search the Add dialog runs) and My requests (status, the
decline reason, author import progress, and withdraw for a pending
request). Any other path sends them to Library, and the shell stops
calling /system/status, the library search and the settings link, all
closed to them server side.

For a requester the Add Author and Add Book confirm steps become one
request step: a format choice and a Request button that posts kind,
foreignId and mediaType. The admin options, and the profile, root folder,
setting and indexer lookups behind them, are never loaded.

Admins get Requests in the nav with a pending count, read once and again
after each decision, never polled. The queue filters by status; Approve
opens an inline form (profile, root folder, monitor and format for an
author, format and search on add for a book) prefilled from the instance
defaults, and Decline takes an optional reason. The Users page role
column becomes an admin, user, requester select, and the create form
offers requester too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* test(smoke): sign in as a requester against the real router

The router is built inline in main(), so only the booted binary proves
the allow list sits on every tree. The smoke suite now creates an admin
through first run setup and a requester through the admin API, signs
the requester in with a cookie and a CSRF token, and checks a grab, an
author read, a file download, a settings read, the Arr compatible queue,
a doubled slash and an encoded slash all answer 403, OPDS by Basic
credentials answers 403, and the requester's own routes answer 200.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* docs: document the requester role, request approval and the OIDC group rule

docs/multi-user.md gains a Requester section: what the role can and
cannot do, how approval works, that it needs the auth mode set to
enabled or proxy, and what tenancy on and off mean for the library a
requester sees. The capability matrix gets a requester column.

docs/auth-oidc.md lists requester as a default role and states the new
group sync rule. docs/auth-proxy.md says there is no header to role
mapping and an admin sets the role after the account exists.
docs/API.md documents the /requests routes, the approval body, the
requester's route surface and the requestCreated webhook fields. README
Features and a changelog fragment round it off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(auth): never let the auth mode elevate a requester, and limit creates and covers

Review of #2670 found that in local-only mode a requester's cookie
request from a LAN address went through ModeGrantsAdmin and was served
as the admin, so the requester could read the API key from
/auth/config and keep it after the mode was switched back. Disabled
mode did the same for every requester.

Middleware now lets a valid session (cookie or proxy) whose role is
requester through as that requester before the mode grant runs, so the
allow list holds in every auth mode. OPDSAuth refuses a requester's
session before its disabled and local-only bypasses in the same way.
What the mode grant does for admin and user sessions is unchanged.

GET /auth/config also stops trusting the context role alone: when the
request names a user, the key is returned only if that user's stored
role is admin. The install itself (API key, an anonymous local client)
still gets it.

The guard's buckets become named limits. POST /requests now spends the
provider bucket (its lookup reaches the provider), and marks the
request charged so a handler that spends the bucket itself does not
charge twice; AllowRequester is that handler side. The image proxy
spends a separate, larger bucket (240, then four a second), because
one library page loads a cover per book.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(api): rate limit request creates, make the pending cap atomic, renew approval claims

Findings from the security review of #2670.

Create spends the provider bucket for a requester before the lookup,
unless the guard already charged the request, so creates with ids the
provider does not know (which store nothing and never fill the cap) are
limited too: the 21st rapid create answers 429.

The pending cap was counted, then a provider round trip, then an insert,
so 24 concurrent creates reached 15 pending against a cap of 3. The
count is now inside the INSERT (and the Reopen UPDATE) as a WHERE
predicate, one statement under SQLite's single writer, and zero rows
affected maps to the existing 429. The earlier count stays as a fast
refusal before the provider call.

A requestCreated for the same owner, kind and foreign id is sent at most
once an hour (in memory, at most 4096 keys), so create and withdraw in a
loop is one webhook.

Approval claims carry a random token and are renewed every third of the
TTL while the add runs; renew, complete and release match the token.
The add cores already return once the author or book row exists and
run the catalogue sync in the background, so the remaining synchronous
work is provider lookups and addBookCore's row poll; renewal covers
those however long they take, and a second approval can no longer
retake the claim and release it under the first. Migration 089 gains
claim_token, and claimed_at moves to milliseconds; 089 has not shipped.

Request and approval bodies now reject any key that is not exactly a
field name, since encoding/json folds case and accepted "Kind" beside
"kind".

Webhook text. The requestCreated sanitiser only replaced @, so <!channel>, <!here>,
<@U123> and [text](https://evil.example) in a provider title or a
username reached the admin's chat channel as live markup.

notifier.SafeText now does the whole job in one place: CleanText (control
and invisible characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, capped), then
@, <, >, [ and ] replaced with fullwidth lookalikes, which read the same
and mean nothing to Discord, Slack, Matrix or markdown. It lives in the
notifier package so any event carrying outside text can use it.
requestCreated uses it for title, author and username; the API's
cleanRequestText delegates to CleanText.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* docs: requester restrictions hold in every auth mode, and the new limits

docs/multi-user.md no longer says the role needs enabled or proxy mode
to restrict anything: a requester's session is never elevated by the
mode, though in disabled and local-only mode a signed out caller is
still the admin, so the advice to use enabled or proxy stays. It also
mentions that creates share the search allowance, covers have their own,
and repeated alerts for one request are suppressed for an hour.
docs/API.md covers the create rate limit and the atomic cap under 429,
the image limit, claim renewal, and the wider webhook sanitising. The
changelog fragment follows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(api): withhold the API key from requesters only, as on main for everyone else

0453d9b1 made GET /auth/config return the API key only when the named
user's stored role was admin. That also hid it from a role user session
that local-only mode stamps admin, a change for existing installs, and
that session can still regenerate the key, so someone who cannot see it
is likely to rotate it and break every integration using the old one.

The rule is now narrower: a request naming a user whose stored role is
requester never gets the key, in any mode. Admin and user behave exactly
as on main. The route test checks a role user session in local-only
mode still receives the key; the unit test's "user stamped admin" case
flips back to receiving it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(db): annotate the two request queries gosec flags as SQL concatenation

The required lint check (golangci-lint v2.11.4 over the whole module)
fails with G202 on the request list query and the library projection
query. Both concatenate only package constants and fixed clauses and
bind every value, so they follow the internal/db convention: a
#nosec G202 comment naming why no input reaches the SQL text.
golangci-lint run ./... now reports 0 issues.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(auth): do not let the mode grant replace a session whose role or epoch cannot be read

Second review of #2670: when the stored role lookup returned empty, or
the session epoch lookup failed, a valid requester cookie fell through
to ModeGrantsAdmin in local-only and disabled mode and was served as the
admin during a database error.

When the mode would grant admin but the request carries a correctly
signed session whose role or epoch could not be read, Middleware now
serves it as that session's user with no role. RestrictRequester holds
an empty role with a user id to the allow list and RequireAdmin refuses
it, so a database error fails closed. A revoked cookie (epoch read and
different) and a request with no cookie are unchanged.

New tests in internal/auth cover both lookup failures in local-only mode
and requester precedence over the mode grant in local-only and disabled
mode, alongside a role user session keeping the admin grant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

* fix(api): release the claim when an approval panics, cap webhooks per requester, unlink URLs

Second review of #2670.

The claim renewer was stopped inline after runApproval, so a panicking
add core (recovered by chi's Recoverer) left the renewer refreshing
claimed_at forever and the request in approving, counted against the
requester's cap, until restart. Approve now stops the renewer in a
defer and, on a panic, releases the claim with its token and re-raises
the panic so Recoverer still logs it. A test with a panicking adder
checks the request is pending again, no renewer is left running, and a
second approval goes through.

Per item suppression let a requester cycle through different ids and
send one requestCreated per create. On top of it, each requester now
triggers at most 10 of those webhooks an hour (in memory, bounded like
the item map); past that the webhook is skipped and one warning is
logged per hour. Requests are still stored and shown.

notifier.SafeText also breaks the "://" of a bare URL with fullwidth
solidi, since Discord, Slack, Telegram and Matrix autolink them. Other
formatting (backticks, underscores) is left alone.

A new repository test puts a request in approving and checks a create
and a reopen at the cap are refused; it fails when the cap predicate
counts only 'pending', a mutation the earlier tests missed.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016fJcCVbNnKsmj2MAAMwWj9
Signed-off-by: vavallee <vavallee@protonmail.com>

commit.message:
Add supervisor role, Teams page and recommended shortcuts (#191)

## Summary

Adds a `supervisor` role and a Teams page. Managers and above group CSRs
under supervisors. Supervisors see their own team across the admin
pages, and the server enforces that scope. Supervisors can also
recommend sources to their team, shown under the label "Recommended",
which replaces "From your team".

**Role and data**
- `lib/db/sql/0004_supervisor_role.sql` adds `supervisor` to
`user_role`, between manager and csr. It ranks 40 (csr 20, manager 60).
- `lib/db/sql/0005_team_members.sql` adds `team_members`. One row per
CSR gives each CSR at most one supervisor.
  - A guard trigger rejects wrong roles and cross-program pairs.
- A cleanup trigger on `users` deletes rows that a role or program
change made invalid.
- Role policy:
  - Managers can create, promote and manage supervisors.
  - Senior managers can manage CSRs, supervisors and managers.
- Supervisors administer no one, except password resets for their own
team.

**Teams page (`/admin/teams`)**
- **Roster view:** a searchable list of CSRs with checkboxes and **Move
to…**. Supervisor team cards and an Unassigned zone are drop targets.
Drag and drop uses `@dnd-kit` (already a dependency) with pointer and
keyboard sensors and screen-reader announcements.
- **Table view:** a per-row supervisor picker, filter pills per team,
select-all and a sticky **Assign supervisor** bar.
- A Roster | Table switch remembers each user's choice.
- Every move updates the page immediately, rolls back and shows the
server's message on failure, and announces the result in a live region.
Requests are capped at the server's 200-person limit per call.
- Supervisors get a read-only view of their own team.

**Supervisor scope (server-enforced)**
- **`GET /api/admin/teams`:** a supervisor gets only their own team,
with `canEdit: false`.
- **`PUT /api/admin/teams/assignments`:**
- Allowed for managers and above; demo accounts are blocked; rate limit
30 per minute.
- Runs in one locked transaction and writes the security event
`team.assign`.
- **`/api/admin/users`:**
- A supervisor lists only their own CSRs and can only reset their
passwords; anyone else returns 404.
  - Every other handler requires manager or above.
  - `role: "supervisor"` is accepted on create and update.
- **`/api/admin/insights/*` (Gaps and Usage):** every per-person read
for a supervisor is filtered to their team (themselves plus their CSRs).
This covers coaching suggestions, view counts and the people list. A
person outside the team returns 404.
- **Navigation:** Gaps, Usage, Users and Teams open to supervisors.
Documents stays manager-only.
- **Page wording:** Usage and Gaps describe the supervisor's team, and
the Gaps review queue (manager-only API) is hidden for supervisors.

**Recommended shortcuts**
- `lib/db/sql/0006_kb_team_shortcuts.sql` adds `kb_team_shortcuts`: a
supervisor's ordered list of sources for their team.
- Guard triggers check that the document belongs to the row's program
and that the owner is a supervisor in that program.
- A cleanup trigger deletes a user's rows when they stop being a
supervisor or change program.
- `GET /api/kb/documents` returns `teamPinPosition` on each item: a
supervisor's own list, or for a CSR, their supervisor's list in the same
program. It also returns `canPinForTeam`, which is true only for
non-demo supervisors.
- `PUT /api/kb/library/team-shortcuts` replaces the caller's list. It is
open to supervisors only, blocks demo accounts, and reuses the 12-source
cap, the locking and the audit pattern of `/featured`.
- In the UI, "From your team" becomes "Recommended". It covers both the
manager's picks for everyone and the supervisor's picks for their team.
The manager's pins use the same wording throughout: "Recommend to
everyone". Supervisors get "Recommend to my team" in the row menu.

**Demo**
- `DEMO_LOGIN_ACCOUNTS` accepts a `supervisor` entry. The login page
lays out one, two or three demo portals.
- `seed:showcase teams` creates the supervisors Renee Alvarez and Priya
Natarajan and renames the demo supervisor to Elliot Brooks. It then
assigns the showcase CSRs across the three teams, leaves one unassigned,
and has Renee and Priya recommend two sources each. The demo supervisor
is a demo account and cannot write, so the seed prints its two sources
for a one-off insert. The step can be run again safely.

## Verification
- `corepack pnpm -r run check`: no errors.
- api-server tests: 362 passed. rag-app tests: 108 passed.
- rag-app build succeeds.
- Built in audited rounds. An independent reviewer reran each round's
checks and read every changed line. Rounds that failed review were fixed
and audited again:
  - coaching suggestions were not limited to the team;
  - the router-level guards had no tests;
  - the seed changed an existing step;
  - the enum position was wrong;
- the Teams page reloaded on unrelated storage events and had no
200-person cap per request;
- the seed tried to write as the demo supervisor, which the server
refuses.
- Codex full review (gpt-6.1-sol, high, 5 sub-reviewers) of f516c80f
found 4 moderate issues, all confirmed and fixed in audited rounds:
- two quick moves on the Teams page could leave one shown on the old
team; moves now go to the server one at a time;
- saving team recommendations could deadlock with a concurrent demotion;
the save now locks the supervisor's row first and rechecks the role;
- the `team.assign` audit event lacked the CSRs moved; it now records
`csrIds` and each one's previous supervisor;
- a keyboard drop lost focus when the dragged row disappeared; focus
falls back to the person's chip or row.
- A second Codex rerun found that two quick "Recommend to my team"
clicks could save out of order and drop the newer pick. Those saves now
go to the server one at a time, and after a failed save the page reloads
only once queued saves have finished.
- Queued saves and Teams moves that have not been sent yet are dropped
when the page closes (sign-out or session expiry), so they cannot go out
under the next user's session.
- A Codex rerun found that deactivating a supervisor left their team
rows, so reactivating them restored a team the page showed as
unassigned. The 0005 cleanup trigger now also clears a supervisor's team
on deactivation.
- CodeQL flagged five admin routes as authorizing without a rate limit.
They now have per-user limits: `GET /api/admin/teams` 60 a minute; users
create, bulk import, update and delete 30 a minute.
- **Not verified:**
  - The SQL has not run against Postgres 18 (only a PGlite smoke test).
- The Teams page has not been used in a browser, because the app does
not run locally.
  - Both are checked on production after deploy (see below).

## Change identity

- Change ID: `TN-CHG-2026-191`
- Change type: `normal`
- Author: `@ryanportfolio`
- Target release/commit: `8f3299af17d7d9466e385366ee27a6272424879c`
- Target environment: `Railway production web and worker services and
pgvector database`
- Significant change: `no`
- Significant-change rationale: `Adds a role below manager and a team
table inside existing program scoping; no new provider, data flow or PCI
scope.`

## Purpose and scope

- Purpose: `Owner request: managers organize CSRs into supervisor teams,
and supervisors see their own team on Usage, Gaps, Users and Teams.`
- Affected components and data boundaries: `lib/db (0004 enum value,
0005 team_members table and triggers, schema.ts enum); api-server:
lib/auth/current-user.ts, lib/auth/demo-accounts.ts, lib/teams.ts,
lib/security/route-rate-limit.ts, routes/admin/teams.ts (new,
/api/admin/teams), routes/admin/users.ts, routes/admin/insights.ts,
routes/index.ts, lib/kb-library.ts, routes/kb.ts, routes/kb-library.ts
(PUT /api/kb/library/team-shortcuts); lib/db 0006 kb_team_shortcuts
table and triggers; rag-app: types/api.ts, lib/api.ts, lib/kbLibrary.ts,
components/kb-library/*, Sidebar, TopBar, AdminUsers, Login, AdminTeams
(new) and components/admin/teams/*, AdminSourceUsage, AdminGaps,
source-usage components; scripts/src/seed-showcase.ts; DESIGN.md,
deployment.md. Data: team_members and kb_team_shortcuts rows scoped by
program_id.`

## Security and PCI impact

- CDE impact: `none`
- CDE-impact rationale: `No payment data; organizational grouping of
existing users.`
- Security impact and threat considered: `Authorization: new role ranked
below manager, so every existing requireManagerOrAbove route stays
closed to supervisors; only teams GET, users GET and reset-password, and
insights open to them. Isolation: supervisor scope is computed
server-side per request from team_members (self plus own CSRs) and
applied to every per-person read in insights; out-of-team ids return
404; program scoping unchanged. Integrity: assignments validated and
locked in one transaction; DB guard trigger enforces roles and program;
cleanup trigger removes stale rows on role or program change. Credential
risk: supervisor password reset limited to own-team CSRs, re-checked
inside the locked transaction. Abuse: 30 writes a minute per user, demo
writes blocked. Audit: team.assign security event in the write
transaction. Recommended shortcuts: the list owner is derived from the
authenticated user only (own list, or the CSR's supervisor via
team_members in the same program); writes are supervisor-only,
demo-blocked, limited to documents visible in the caller's program,
capped at 12, and audited as kb.library.team_shortcuts.set; DB triggers
enforce document program and supervisor role.`

## PCI DSS 6.5 change controls

- 6.5.1 bespoke/custom security testing: `completed`
- 6.5.1 evidence or rationale: `Unit tests for role policy, supervisor
reset authorization, router-level and per-route guards
(mutation-checked), team-scope SQL rendering, assignment schema;
independent audits of every per-user read in insights; Codex review.`
- 6.5.2 completion revalidation: `not applicable`
- 6.5.2 evidence owner and plan/result: `No PCI control or scope
change.`
- 6.5.3 pre-production separation: `not applicable`
- 6.5.3 evidence or rationale: `There is no separate pre-production
environment; verified by tests and build, then production API checks
after deploy.`
- 6.5.4 role/function separation: `not applicable`
- 6.5.4 evidence or accountability rationale: `Single-owner repository
has no truthful non-author reviewer identity. CI, independent audit
rounds and the Codex review supply technical gates.`
- 6.5.5 live PAN in pre-production: `no live PAN`
- 6.5.5 evidence or rationale: `No payment data handled.`
- 6.5.6 test data/accounts removal: `not applicable`
- 6.5.6 evidence owner and plan/result: `Demo supervisors are intended
demo data in the demo program, like the existing showcase CSRs.`

## Verification

- Commands and results: `pnpm -r run check pass; api-server test 362
pass; rag-app test 108 pass; rag-app build pass; scripts check pass.`
- Negative/security tests: `CSR refused by role guards; supervisor
refused on manager routes; supervisor reset limited to own team;
out-of-scope userId helper; team-shortcuts role rule for all five roles
and schema rejects (cap, duplicates, bad uuid, extra field); demo writes
blocked (existing middleware). PGlite smoke of 0006 triggers:
cross-program document, non-supervisor owner and cross-program owner
refused; cleanup on role or program change.`
- Runtime/integration verification: `Pending: after deploy, as demo
supervisor GET /api/admin/teams returns only own team with canEdit
false; source-usage people only team; out-of-team userId 404; PUT
assignments 403; out-of-team reset 404; as agent super user a move
persists and is restored.`
- Evidence not collected locally: `SQL apply on Postgres 18 and browser
use of the Teams page.`

## Vulnerabilities and dependencies

- Dependency/SBOM impact: `None: no new dependencies.`
- Finding/exception links: `None.`

## Deployment and secure recovery

- Deployment/configuration/DDL steps: `After merge, with the owner's go
(given): railway-apply-sql 0004, then 0005, then 0006 (separate runs);
add a supervisor entry to DEMO_LOGIN_ACCOUNTS on web and worker with
--skip-deploys; railway up web and worker from main; seed:showcase
teams; one-off insert of the demo supervisor's two recommended sources.`
- Post-deployment verification: `/health ok; schema_migrations has 0004,
0005 and 0006; team_members and kb_team_shortcuts exist with their
triggers; the API checks above; a seeded supervisor's recommended
sources carry teamPinPosition for a CSR on that team and not for a CSR
on another team; PUT /api/kb/library/team-shortcuts as a non-supervisor
returns 403; /admin/teams, /admin/sources, /admin/gaps, /admin/users
load for manager and supervisor.`
- Failure signal: `SQL apply fails, /health fails, or any supervisor API
check returns data outside the team.`
- Secure recovery procedure: `Redeploy the previous Railway deployment.
0006 and 0005 can be reverted by dropping kb_team_shortcuts,
team_members and their triggers and functions; the enum value in 0004
cannot be dropped in place and is harmless when unused (no users hold it
after demoting them).`
- Incident ID: `Not applicable: normal change`
- Emergency authority: `Not applicable: normal change`
- Retrospective review due: `Not applicable: normal change`

## Approval and closure

- Non-author reviewer: `Unassigned: no truthful distinct reviewer
identity exists in the repository; owner requested this change.`
- Review evidence: `This pull request, its hosted checks, and the Codex
review recorded on it.`

Phase 0 of the two-wave refactor. Covers backend and frontend: ranked
findings with evidence, DB access layer recommendation, Express to Fastify
migration plan, Pinia design, ESLint flat config and Prettier plan, the

Formatting only. Verified behavior-neutral: esbuild-minified output of all
