Unused imports, variables, types and component registrations; statement
ternaries to if/else; explicit emits declarations on the form field and
search components; empty interfaces to type aliases; unused catch bindings;
promise-handling findings in the backend shutdown path, scrape limiter and
Playwright route handler; Error.captureStackTrace without a local cast.

* ci: enforce lint and format checks with a suppression baseline

Add lint and format check steps to both CI jobs. The remaining violations
that need behavior changes (prop mutation, component naming, direct
transport imports in two views, <script setup> in two files, and the
application-to-middleware import) are baselined in eslint-suppressions.json.
Document the tooling in the README and backend setup guide, and list the
formatting commit in .git-blame-ignore-revs.

* refactor: drop leftover unused import in PieChart

* refactor: extract createApp from server.ts

Move-only. src/app.ts builds the Express application (middleware, routers,
health probes, error pipeline) without listening or touching the process;
server.ts keeps env loading, database open, listen and shutdown. Verified by
starting the server against a throwaway database: health, readiness and the
404 envelope respond as before.

* refactor: allow injecting sales sources and more-info collaborators into createApp

Optional dependencies with the current implementations as defaults, so the
SSE routes can be exercised with fakes instead of live scrapers and OpenAI.

* test: add HTTP contract suite on a real SQLite database

Transport-agnostic harness (TestClient + supertest adapter) and contract
tests for every route group: platform, auth, plants, substrates, components,
watering, images, sales and more-info SSE, plus a 401/403 inventory over all
authenticated routes. Known defects from the audit are pinned in 'known
defects' blocks and flip when fixed. Backend line coverage 64.4% to 86.7%;
CI now runs the coverage gate.

* test: frontend characterization suite and coverage gate

Tests for UserService (token storage, refresh retries, identity getters),
ApiUtils request engine (headers, null body, refresh gate, SSE ticket),
PlantService, WateringService, SubstrateService, SalesService, the markdown
converter in MoreInfoService, the router table and guard, and the generic
form components. 117 new tests; frontend line coverage 11.7% to 29.1% with a
threshold gate wired into CI. vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 move to 4.1.11.

Also corrects the BUG-05 description in the audit: the logout() call after a
failed refresh is unreachable because handleRequest rethrows first.

* build(backend): update vulnerable dependencies

axios 1.20, multer 2.4, sharp 0.35.5, express-rate-limit 8.7, supertest 7.3,
tsx 4.23, vite 8.3 (vitest stays on 4.1.11). Transitive advisories in
path-to-regexp, qs, body-parser, proxy-addr and ip-address are resolved by the
refreshed lockfile; brace-expansion is pinned through an override. nodemon
(chokidar/braces, no patched release) is replaced by tsx watch for the dev
script. pnpm audit reports no vulnerabilities.

* build(frontend): update vulnerable dependencies

vue 3.5.43, vue-router 5.4, @ionic/vue 8.8.19, vite 8.3, plugin-vue/legacy,
@vue/test-utils 2.5, eslint-plugin-vue 10.11, vue-tsc 3.3.12, @capacitor/cli
8.5, cypress 15.21. Transitive advisories in undici (kept on 7.x for jsdom),
tar, qs, xmldom, source-map-js, postcss-selector-parser and brace-expansion
are pinned through pnpm overrides; the ineffective npm-style overrides block
is removed. pnpm audit --prod reports nothing; two dev-only findings remain
without a compatible fix (braces via eslint tooling, uuid in the Capacitor
CLI's xcode helper).

* feat(backend): session ids, central guest policy, entity-scoped image access, ticketed sales stream

Sessions carry a sid shared by access and refresh tokens, so logout, password change and eviction end the access token too. Guests get a separate session policy so concurrent guests no longer evict each other. Guest read-only is enforced once before the routers. Plant and substrate reads, and every image route, check the caller against the owning entity. The sales stream requires a ticket. Auth and AI stream endpoints are rate limited per user. Falsy user id 0 is no longer treated as missing.

* docs(backend): document session, status code and authorization contract

* fix(frontend): refresh the session only on 401

* test(backend): cover the rate limiter factory

* fix(backend): answer client errors with 4xx, add input limits, surface AI stream failures

Body parser and SQLite constraint failures map to 400, 409 or 413 instead of 500. Disallowed CORS origins no longer fail the request. Undecodable uploads answer 400. Registration and profile changes enforce username 3 to 64 characters and password 8 characters up to 72 bytes; login stays lenient for existing accounts. Substrate and component names are capped at 100 characters. OpenAI failures and a missing key end the stream with an error event, and server-side HTML formatting escapes model output.

* docs(backend): document error mapping and input limits

* fix(frontend): escape model output before rendering and show validation messages

The markdown converter HTML-escapes the buffer before applying inline rules. Registration errors read the V2 error envelope (fields, conflict message) instead of the V1 requirements array.

* refactor(backend): typed config module, core/auth, drop express-async-handler

core/config/env.ts is the only reader of process.env and validates required variables. Token and session logic moves out of core/middleware into core/auth, which removes the application-to-middleware dependency. Express 5 forwards rejected handler promises, so the wrapper and its dependency go; the one manually invoked image handler now awaits.

* refactor(backend): move species matching into a domain resolver, drop dead sales SseManager

The fuzzy species matching and its cache leave SQLitePlantRepository. SpeciesResolver is a pure domain service over a SpeciesCatalog port, with a SQLite catalog adapter and its own unit tests. The unused modules/sales/presentation/SseManager is deleted.

* refactor(backend): type the SSE writer against ServerResponse; update architecture docs

* refactor(backend): Kysely query layer, versioned migrations and a tested dump importer

Repositories use typed Kysely queries behind unchanged ports. An idempotent baseline migration replaces initSchema and ensureSchemaExtensions, so existing databases simply record it. The server awaits initDatabase before listening. Repository tests run against an in-memory database built by the migrations; the hand-wired mocked integration tests are removed because the contract suite covers them. The species catalog port becomes async.

scripts/migrate-sqlite.js is replaced by src/tools/importMysqlDump.ts (pnpm run db:import). It builds the target through the migrations, lets dump rows replace seed rows (the old script aborted on colliding roles or guest user), matches species ignoring case, names the failing dump statement, and has a fixture dump test.

* docs(backend): document the Kysely layer, migrations and the dump import

* fix(backend): clean up images with their entity, store relative image paths, order and transact

Deleting a plant, substrate or component now removes its image rows and files through an EntityImageCleanup port. Migration 0002 purges existing orphan rows (and their files); migration 0003 stores image urls as origin-free paths, with the origin added on read from PUBLIC_BASE_URL or the request, so responses stay absolute. Images are read oldest first with an id tiebreak. Plant create and update share one transaction with the species insert. An accepted empty scrape page is cached; a page every strategy failed on is not.

* refactor(backend): migrate the HTTP layer from Express to Fastify 5

Transport swap behind an unchanged contract: the only contract test file that changes is harness.ts, which now drives the app with Fastify inject. app.ts becomes an async buildApp registering encapsulated route plugins; auth, guest read-only, admin and ticket checks are hooks that throw AppErrors; one error handler and one not-found handler keep the error envelope; a lenient JSON parser keeps empty and null bodies working and maps malformed JSON to 400; @fastify/cookie, cors, rate-limit (several buckets per route), multipart (buffered, 10 MB cap) and static replace their Express counterparts; SSE hijacks the reply and carries over earlier headers; request ids are validated before being echoed. express, cors, cookie-parser, express-rate-limit, multer, supertest and their types are removed.

* docs(backend): describe the Fastify HTTP layer

* refactor(frontend): add Pinia and move the session into a store

The session store owns the token, identity getters, login, guest login, logout, profile changes and a single-flight token refresh (concurrent 401s share one request). The transport no longer imports a service: ApiUtils receives a refresh and teardown bridge at startup, which removes the apiUtils/UserService and UserService/router import cycles. The router guard reads the store, and components read identity from store getters instead of awaiting service calls. Logout resets every store and the legacy cache. UserService is removed.

* refactor(frontend): move plants into a Pinia store with L2 persistence

The plants store holds the list, derived personal and public lists as getters, and optimistic create, edit and delete built on a shared optimistic helper (item-scoped rollback). A small persistence plugin writes selected state to the Ionic storage in the existing envelope and hydrates it on demand; resets cancel pending writes so a logout cannot leave an empty fresh entry behind. Views bind to store getters instead of listening for document events. PlantService is removed.

* refactor(frontend): move watering into a Pinia store

Records per plant and the fertilizer types live in one store with optimistic add, edit and delete that never touch other plants' entries. The persistence plugin now supports several entries and an explicit snapshot time, which keeps the two existing cache keys. Deleting a plant drops its watering records through the store. WateringRecords derives its records, last watering and options from store getters. WateringService is removed.

* refactor(frontend): move substrates and components into Pinia stores

Both catalogues load through ensureLoaded with shared requests and persist under their existing cache keys. Substrate mutations stay pessimistic and upsert the server's version; component admin mutations upsert or remove. The plants store looks substrate names up in the substrates store, and the plant, substrate and component views bind to store getters instead of document events. Deleting or editing a component no longer depends on a truthy response, so a 204 answer completes the flow. SubstrateService and ComponentService are removed.

* refactor(frontend): move sales, more-info, admin health and calendar to Pinia; remove BaseService

Sales and more-info streams build up a draft and commit only on completion, so a failed stream never persists partial data. Calendar settings are persistent and never expire; admin source health stays live. The Markdown renderer becomes a pure utility. TabsPage and App.vue become Options API components. The persistence plugin only writes entries whose data changed and, for entries with a fetch time, only once they have one, so a store that is merely loading cannot overwrite a good snapshot. BaseService, the document event bus and the remaining services are removed; ImageService is a plain module. import-x/no-cycle is enforced again.

* fix(frontend): register the debug route only in development, stop mutating props in modals

The debug view (demo credentials, direct service calls) is no longer routable in production builds. ImageEditingModal and ImageUploadModal no longer write to their isOpen prop, and ComponentSelection reports part changes to its parent instead of mutating the object it was given. Debug no longer imports the transport layer.

* docs: bring backend and frontend documentation in line with the code, add wave 1 summary

* docs: wave 2 frontend UX audit (#34)

* chore: isolated dev-up and dev-down with mocked scrapers, AI guide and seed data

* fix(backend): answer CORS preflights for PUT, PATCH and DELETE

@fastify/cors 11 defaults to GET, HEAD and POST, so a frontend on another origin could not edit or delete. The methods are explicit and a contract test sends the preflights.

* feat(frontend): botanical redesign with states, watering-first details and PWA

Tokens and dark mode, plant-tag cards and authored placeholders, StateBlock for every list and detail, watering status with Water now and Undo, inline validated forms, outlined fields, sales tab, persistent desktop menu, service worker and offline banner, per-plant watering state in the list.

* docs: product record, design system, wave 2 summary and critique

PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the direction contract, the design critique snapshot and the wave 2 summary; frontend design system and store docs.

* chore: seed every watering state, a second public owner and search source health

Plants cover ok, due, overdue, watered today and never watered; a collector account owns public items for the Public tab; a seven component substrate covers the component search; link search sources fill the admin health screen. CLAUDE.md lists what each seeded item is for.

* feat(frontend): round 2 critique fixes for modals, admin screens and the Sales list

One dialog and field system with visible typed confirmation and inert disabled buttons, consequence text and Undo for deletes, substrate wizard steps, reminders flow, admin recheck results inline with status strip and technical details, Sales cards with price and discount, German enum labels, plurals and dates, themed scrollbars, 44px targets. Dev stack lifts sign-in limits and seeds leaf photos.

* chore: ignore fake test and mock-data credentials in GitGuardian scans

Release 0.1.1 (#10) * Require a real browser session in the dashboard The web server fell back to METRUNE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN whenever no metrune_session cookie was present, so an anonymous visitor to the development stack was served as an organization admin. The same fallback reached the /api/admin/* proxy routes, where an unauthenticated POST created real records. The signed-in session is now the only credential the dashboard forwards, and isSessionToken additionally refuses a cookie holding a service token: the API resolves dashboard tokens before browser sessions, so a known met_ token in the cookie would otherwise authorize organization reads and mutations. Middleware answers before anything renders, which also stops the organization name leaking through the shell while a page-level redirect was still streaming. Page requests get a 307 to /login and /api/* gets 401 JSON. Demo-fixture mode is deleted rather than gated. It was unreachable in practice, because the token fallback meant the live fetch never failed, and dropping it collapses Result to the T | null convention the rest of the module already used. A failed read now also logs, since an "unavailable" panel was otherwise indistinguishable from a transient upstream failure. The session cookie's Secure flag moves from NODE_ENV to METRUNE_ENV. The production build sets NODE_ENV=production even in the development stack, which marked the cookie Secure over http://localhost; Safari discards that and sign-in failed silently, looping back to /login. * Stop issuing a dev dashboard token and bind the dev stack to loopback compose.yaml handed the web service met_dashboard_dev, the seeded admin-role token that made anonymous browsing possible, and published both ports on 0.0.0.0 while the README only asked operators not to expose the stack. The token is gone, METRUNE_ENABLE_DEMO_DATA with it, and the ports now bind 127.0.0.1 so the request is enforced rather than made. check-production-compose.sh grew the matching assertions and now covers the development file too: both compose files must publish exactly two loopback ports, and neither may give the web service a dashboard token. Verified by reintroducing each fault and confirming the check fails. * Scope session drilldown and export by role instead of by credential type /v1/analytics/sessions refused every user session outright, so the organization drilldown was reachable only with a service token. The dashboard's Export button therefore returned 403 for real users in development and 503 in production: it had never worked for anyone. Meanwhile analytics_session_detail scoped every user session to owner_user_id, so lifting the list restriction alone would have let an admin list sessions it then got 404 opening. Both endpoints now share DashboardAuth::session_owner_scope. An analyst or admin reads the whole organization; every other role is scoped to the rows it owns; a viewer's service token has no user identity to scope by and is refused. /api/export follows the same rule and names the file for the scope it returned. * Read Claude Code usage from the nested message object Claude Code writes token counts under message.usage, but the shared extractor only looked at usage.*, tokens.*, and top-level input_tokens. Every record scored zero tokens and was dropped by the tokens.total() == 0 guard, so Claude Code sessions never appeared at all while Codex worked fine. The nesting was already known for two neighbouring fields: role reads message.role and model_id reads message.model. Usage was simply missed. The existing fixture hid it by writing a flat shape with role at the top level, which Claude Code has never produced. The new test uses a record copied verbatim from a real transcript. Against nine real transcripts the fix extracts 2,266 usage messages where it previously found none. * Make the macOS client installable, reconfigurable and gated Four separate obstacles on macOS: The installer assumed /usr/local/bin exists. A stock macOS has no such directory and BSD install will not create one, so the install failed on its own temp file with "No such file or directory". It now creates the destination, escalating only when it must. The classifier could only be set during enroll. Fixing a typo'd model meant re-enrolling and minting a second installation, and `classifier provision` silently discarded a locally configured profile whenever the organization had none of its own - reporting it as "Classification is disabled", which reads as informational rather than destructive. There is now `classifier configure`, reusing the code path enroll ends with, and provision only clears a profile the organization owns. `scan` skipped unchanged sources with no way to override, so re-reading after a fix was impossible; `scan --force` re-reads everything. Replaying cannot double-count because the server replaces by session key and revision. test-e2e.sh assumed GNU userland and the Linux artifact. It now detects the host, builds the client from the checkout on macOS, and uses portable sha256/stat/date helpers. Note the hermetic HOME override means macOS cannot resolve a login keychain, so the run always takes the 0600 fallback; the system-keyring path is covered instead by an ignored test that asserts the storage mode and so fails on a silent fallback, wired into both native release legs where publishing already depends on it. * Let a workspace without SMTP add and recover members A self-hosted install with no mail transport was a dead end. Inviting returned 503, the public reset endpoint answered 202 and sent nothing, and production refused to boot at all without SMTP - so the evaluator or small team who skipped mail could never add a second person, and anyone who forgot a password was locked out permanently. Invitations are now created either way. With a mailer the behaviour and response are unchanged and no token is returned; without one the accept link comes back for the administrator to deliver, and resend re-issues it since it already rotated the token. The status is reported as "manual" rather than "sending" so the dashboard offers resend and revoke; a manual invitation was otherwise stuck, being neither re-linkable nor cancellable. The public reset endpoint keeps answering 202 for every address - that is anti-enumeration and can never hand back a token - so recovery is administrator-initiated instead, scoped to the caller's organization. Production no longer refuses to start without SMTP; it warns and names what the operator gave up. Running without mail is a deployment choice. A partially configured relay is still rejected, because that is a mistake rather than a choice. This does widen who sees an invitation token: on a mailless server it passes through the administrator's browser and clipboard rather than existing only in the recipient's mailbox. An admin can already invite any address at any role, so the delta is small, but it is a deliberate change to the invite threat model. * Cover the boundaries these changes depend on The suite only ever probed /profile unauthenticated, so the anonymous dashboard went unnoticed. It now asserts that every route redirects and carries no organization data, that the admin proxies reject both an anonymous write and a service token in the session cookie, that the development cookie is not marked Secure over http, that an admin's export is organization-scoped, and that an invite without SMTP is delivered by link and accepted by a real second browser context. The invitation test runs last: placed earlier it perturbed the admin lifecycle test's team create/delete. Removing it made that test pass and reordering keeps the suite green, but the coupling itself is undiagnosed and could resurface. * Update the docs to match the changed behaviour The dashboard credential fallback and demo fixtures are gone, drilldown and export are role-scoped, invitations and administrator resets work without SMTP, and the client gained classifier configure and scan --force. The docs described none of it, and several statements had become wrong: SMTP listed as a production requirement, invitations as email-only, and the export as unconditionally organization-wide. Also records what is still not covered, rather than implying otherwise: the macOS E2E path exists but is not a release gate, Windows enrollment is uncovered, and watch mode is uncovered everywhere. Adds the classifier-model guidance that was missing entirely - the protocol and JSON requirements, and the built-in local default. * Trigger releases by hand from the committed version Releases were cut by pushing a server-vX.Y.Z or client-vX.Y.Z tag, which made the tag the thing an operator typed and the version something that had to agree with it. The client workflow had no manual trigger at all, so a client release could not be run without pushing a tag, and the server workflow took a free-text version input that could disagree with the committed one. Both workflows now dispatch only. A version job reads the committed package version, derives the namespaced tag from it, and the publishing job creates that tag on the released commit. Nobody types a version or a tag, so the two cannot drift apart. Manual runs are refused from any branch other than the default one, and a concurrency group keeps two operators from racing the same release. assert-release-tag-available.sh proves a tag is absent before the release proceeds. It distinguishes git ls-remote's "queried fine, no such ref" status from transport and authentication failures, so a broken lookup stops the release rather than reading as an available tag. release-draft.sh uploads into a commit-bound draft, verifies the exact asset set, rechecks the tag, and only then publishes. A draft holds no Git ref, so an interrupted upload resumes instead of claiming or moving the tag. Server image tags are promoted only after both images have passed scanning and attestation, and an existing tag is never moved to a different digest. The ci.yml and security.yml trigger comments described the tag push that no longer exists; they now say the release gate consumes those checks from the release commit on main. * Give the invitation and reset emails a real layout Both messages were a bare run of

tags, so they arrived as unstyled text with a default-blue underlined link and nothing identifying them as Metrune. They now share one layout() built from the dashboard palette: a centred card, a heading, the call to action, and the raw link repeated underneath for clients that mangle anchors. The button is a table cell carrying bgcolor rather than a styled anchor, because Outlook drops background colours on links, and every rule is inline because mail clients strip

feat(consent): T&C residual audit bundle (WORM ledger + middleware fail-closed + WS mid-session re-check) (#3853)

* chore: initialize feat-oauth-tc-consent-3205

* docs: capture brainstorm and spec for feat-oauth-tc-consent-3205

Brainstorm pivot — original #3205 premise (no server-side T&C
enforcement on OAuth callback) is stale. Server-side enforcement
shipped via PR #898 + #927 + migrations 005-008 on 2026-03-20.

Triad audit (CLO + CPO + CTO) of shipped implementation surfaced 6
residual gaps:
- R1 append-only tc_acceptances ledger (brand-survival; GDPR Art 7.1)
- R2 middleware fail-closed on DB error
- R3 WS mid-session re-check after TC_VERSION bump
- R4 CI guardrail vs silent T&C edit drift
- R5 bundled-consent UI checkbox-copy verify
- R6 e2e coverage of OAuth -> /accept-terms -> /dashboard

Bundled-PR scope chosen. spec.md frontmatter:
  lane: cross-domain
  brand_survival_threshold: single-user incident
  requires_clo_signoff: true
  requires_cpo_signoff: true

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(learnings): walk migration history before designing a fix for schema-domain issues

Captures the pattern surfaced in #3205 brainstorm: when an issue cites a gap
in a domain with persistent state, walk the migration directory for
*remediate_*, *remove_*_trust, *backfill_* filenames before spawning
domain leaders. A 10-minute migration scan can detect that the entire
enforcement surface has already shipped + been remediated, which pivots
the brainstorm from "design the fix" to "audit residual gaps."

Ref #3205, PR #3853

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: create plan and tasks for feat-oauth-tc-consent-3205

Plan-review revision applied (DHH + Kieran + simplicity converged):

Cuts (multi-reviewer agreement):
- Collapse 6-artifact build-time SHA pipeline -> 1 hand-edited literal
  in tc-version.ts + 1 CI guardrail script. Drop: compute-tc-sha.mjs,
  tc-document-sha.generated.ts, prebuild/pretest hooks, .gitignore
  entry, re-export shim, runtime SHA test, bash test driver.
- Defer pg_cron retention sweep (0 beta users + 7-year horizon means
  sweep runs against 0 rows until 2033). Column stays; sweep is filed
  as deferred-tracking issue at Phase 10.2.
- Drop migration parse-test theater (literal-string presence); keep
  only the REVOKE four-role pattern grep + INVOKER trigger assert.
- Drop Phase 9.3 learning-addendum; PR description carries the
  cross-reference.

Kieran P0 fixes:
- tool_use is server->client only; gate list corrected to inbound
  types (start_session, resume_session, chat,
  interactive_prompt_response, review_gate_response); abort_turn +
  close_conversation exempt.
- AC9 reworded: mocked tests cannot prove server-side atomicity;
  assertion is "route handler delegates to one RPC."
- Idempotency moved to RPC via UNIQUE(user_id, version) + ON CONFLICT
  DO NOTHING; route handler early-return removed (race-fix).

Polish:
- AC10 covers all 3 TC_EXEMPT_PATHS via test.each.
- Trigger function REVOKEs from service_role too (four-role).
- RPC body uses server-side now() exclusively; no client-supplied
  timestamp.

Codebase reconciliation (RC1-RC8):
- WS_CLOSE_CODES.TC_NOT_ACCEPTED already imported at
  ws-handler.ts:1851 -> drop "literal 4004 rename" task.
- /accept-terms + /signup checkbox copy already meets GDPR Art. 7(2)
  bar -> FR7 downgraded to regression-prevention assertion only.
- 043 migration is the gold-standard WORM ledger precedent ->
  mirror schema shape + Art. 17 anonymise RPC.
- Supabase default-privileges trap (learning 2026-05-06) requires
  four-role REVOKE.
- TC_EXEMPT_PATHS has 3 entries, not 2.

Brand-survival threshold: single-user incident (GDPR Art. 7(1)).
CPO sign-off carry-forward from brainstorm; CLO sign-off required
at PR review on schema + rubric + retention default.

Ref #3205, PR #3853

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(legal): sync plugin T&C site copy body to canonical

Updates plugins/soleur/docs/pages/legal/terms-and-conditions.md body to
match docs/legal/terms-and-conditions.md at Last Updated April 10, 2026
(Section 8.1c Shared Content terms - longer 'Revocation' + 'No warranty
of recipient conduct' language). Preserves Eleventy frontmatter +
page-hero/content section scaffolding + {{ stats.* }} template vars +
/legal/ link rewrites + www.soleur.ai contact URL.

Refs #3205. Required precondition for PR #3853 CI guardrail
(.github/workflows/ci.yml tc-document-sha-guard) introduced in
Phase 6 of the residual-audit bundle. Canonical doc is the legal
source of record; plugin site rewrites links and wraps the body in
Eleventy presentational markup.

The CI guardrail (Phase 6 of plan) normalizes link forms and template
vars before comparison rather than enforcing strict byte-equality.

* feat(migration): 044 tc_acceptances WORM ledger + accept_terms RPC

Append-only T&C consent ledger for GDPR Art. 7(1) demonstrability.
Mirrors 043 (tenant_deploy_audit) structure: RLS zero-policies,
WORM trigger with single Art. 17 anonymise bypass, SECURITY DEFINER
RPCs with public-first search_path pin and four-role REVOKE pattern
(2026-05-06-supabase-default-privileges-defeat-revoke-from-public.md).

accept_terms(p_user_id, p_version, p_doc_sha) is idempotent at the
RPC layer: UPDATE public.users is a no-op when tc_accepted_version
already matches; INSERT into tc_acceptances uses ON CONFLICT
(user_id, version) DO NOTHING. The route handler always calls this
RPC -- no early-return on already-current version (plan Kieran P0-3).

anonymise_tc_acceptances(p_user_id) UPDATEs user_id = NULL on
matching rows to preserve audit-trail row count for legal
demonstrability while satisfying Art. 17 erasure. Holds the single
SET-site for app.tc_acceptances_anonymise_in_progress.

WORM trigger function is INVOKER (not DEFINER) so current_user
reflects the calling role -- DEFINER would always evaluate to
postgres and break the legitimate Art. 17 bypass.

No pg_cron retention sweep in v1 (deferred): 0 beta users +
7-year window means the sweep runs against 0 rows for years.
retention_until column ships for forward-compat (AC21 tracks
the deferred sweep follow-on).

Test surface: trigger-fn-specific lint at
test/migration-044-tc-acceptances.test.ts; SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
covered automatically by the generalised
test/migration-rpc-grants.test.ts (76 tests, all green).

Refs #3205. Plan:
knowledge-base/project/plans/2026-05-15-feat-oauth-tc-consent-residual-audit-plan.md

* feat(api): accept-terms delegates to accept_terms RPC

Drops the route-handler idempotency early-return (SELECT
tc_accepted_version then short-circuit if already current). The
new public.accept_terms(p_user_id, p_version, p_doc_sha) RPC owns
idempotency via ON CONFLICT (user_id, version) DO NOTHING +
same-value UPDATE no-op. Route always calls the RPC -- consistent
with Kieran P0-3 of the plan.

Adds TC_DOCUMENT_SHA hand-edited literal to lib/legal/tc-version.ts
(SHA-256 of docs/legal/terms-and-conditions.md at HEAD). Persisted
per acceptance in tc_acceptances.document_sha so the audit ledger
captures exactly which document the user accepted. Drift policy
documented in the JSDoc; CI guardrail
(.github/workflows/ci.yml :: tc-document-sha-guard) lands in
Phase 6.

Test surface: api-accept-terms-ledger.test.ts (6 tests, all GREEN)
proves the route handler calls .rpc("accept_terms", ...) exactly
once with (p_user_id, p_version, p_doc_sha), does NOT write users
or tc_acceptances directly, does NOT short-circuit on already-
current version, surfaces RPC errors to Sentry via
reportSilentFallback, and preserves the CSRF + auth gates.

Refs #3205.

* fix(middleware): fail closed on tcError, redirect to accept-terms

middleware.ts:133-138 previously logged tcError and continued with
NextResponse.next() — a silent fail-open. During a Supabase outage,
every authenticated user reached /dashboard without server-side
T&C verification, an Art. 7(1) demonstrability breach (plan
§"User-Brand Impact"). Brand-survival single-user-incident class.

New behaviour on tcError != null for non-exempt paths:
  1. reportSilentFallback() to Sentry with feature=middleware,
     op=tc_query_failed (gives ops a paging signal).
  2. Redirect to /accept-terms?error=db_unavailable.

The exempt-path short-circuit at line 126 still fires above this
branch, so /accept-terms, /api/accept-terms, and
/api/auth/github-resolve/callback remain reachable during a
DB incident — users can still see the accept-terms page and the
github-resolve recovery path stays open.

redirectWithCookies gains an optional searchParams arg so the
db_unavailable signal survives the cookie-preserving redirect.

Test surface: middleware.fail-closed.test.ts (5 tests, all GREEN):
  - test.each(TC_EXEMPT_PATHS) asserts no redirect on tcError
    (a 4th exempt path automatically gets covered).
  - /dashboard asserts 307/308 → /accept-terms?error=db_unavailable.
  - reportSilentFallback shape assertion.

Existing middleware.test.ts CSP coverage invariant still GREEN
(redirectWithCookies path is recognised).

Refs #3205.

* feat(ws-handler): mid-session T&C re-check with 30s cache

Inbound message types start_session, resume_session, chat,
interactive_prompt_response, review_gate_response now re-validate
users.tc_accepted_version against TC_VERSION mid-session.
WS_CLOSE_CODES.TC_NOT_ACCEPTED (4004) on stale consent or DB
error. abort_turn + close_conversation are EXEMPT per RC8 of the
plan: a user must always be able to stop a stream or close a
conversation even with stale consent.

Before this change, the WS handshake-only check at line 1850 left
long-running streams against a stale consent version after a
TC_VERSION bump — brand-survival single-user incident class.

Per-session 30 s cache (TC_RECHECK_CACHE_MS) bounds DB load. Trade-
off: up to 30 s of stale-consent traffic after a bump may pass
before the next gated message closes the socket. Explicit in
plan AC6 + AC11.

recheckTcMidSession is exported for test isolation; handleMessage
invokes it above the switch so the helper covers every gated
inbound type without per-case duplication.

ClientSession gains tcVersionAtHandshake (handshake baseline) and
tcRecheckCacheUntil (cache expiry). Both seeded at session
registration from the same users SELECT that already runs.

Test surface: ws-handler.tc-mid-session.test.ts (16 tests, GREEN):
  - test.each(GATED_TYPES) stale-version close.
  - test.each(GATED_TYPES) current-version no-close.
  - test.each(EXEMPT_TYPES) stale-version no-close (no DB query).
  - 30 s cache: 2 messages in window → 1 SELECT.
  - cache expiry: messages past TTL → SELECT runs again.
  - TC_RECHECK_CACHE_MS == 30_000 (constant assertion).
  - DB SELECT error → fail-closed (socket closed).

Refs #3205.

* ci(tc-document-sha-guard): guard mirror drift + sha staleness

Three invariants enforced per PR:
  1. docs/legal/terms-and-conditions.md (canonical, jurisdiction:
     FR/EU markdown source of record for tc_acceptances.document_sha)
     and plugins/soleur/docs/pages/legal/terms-and-conditions.md (the
     Eleventy mirror rendered at soleur.ai/legal/terms-and-conditions/)
     have identical NORMALISED prose bodies.
     Normalisation strips: Eleventy frontmatter, page-hero/content
     section scaffolding, link form (.md vs /legal/<name>/), template-
     var expressions ({{ stats.agents }} etc.), the canonical's top-
     level "# Terms & Conditions" heading. A presentation refactor
     stays equal; a body content drift fails.
  2. TC_DOCUMENT_SHA is a 64-char lowercase hex literal in
     apps/web-platform/lib/legal/tc-version.ts.
  3. TC_DOCUMENT_SHA equals sha256(canonical doc) unless the same PR
     also bumped TC_VERSION (bump-policy escape hatch: a SHA change
     implies the operator inspected the diff and either decided
     cosmetic → no version bump → CI requires manual literal update,
     OR material/clarifying → TC_VERSION bumped).

Surfaces drift as a hard CI failure with remediation steps. GHA job
runs on every PR via actions/checkout fetch-depth: 0 so the
origin/<base>...HEAD git diff sees TC_VERSION lines.

Negative-case verification (operator-side):
  $ echo "drift" >> docs/legal/terms-and-conditions.md
  $ bash apps/web-platform/scripts/check-tc-document-sha.sh
  # ::error::T&C body drift: ... → exit 1

asserts both /accept-terms and /signup pages contain the literals

×four literals. If a future PR strips one of the document names
or merges the two anchor URLs into a single combined link, this
fires before review. GDPR Art. 7(2) "distinguishable" bar.

P8 (AC9 / Phase 8): end-to-end vitest covering OAuth-callback →
/accept-terms → RPC. Mocks supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession +
getUser + service-client SELECT (workspace_status,
tc_accepted_version) + accept_terms RPC. Three tests:

  1. GET /(auth)/callback with NULL tc_accepted_version → 307/308

  2. POST /api/accept-terms → service .rpc("accept_terms", {p_user_id,

     no .from("tc_acceptances") on the service client.
  3. Composite flow asserting both endpoints together with shared
     fixture user.

Per Kieran P0-2: the assertion is "the route delegates to one RPC",
not "the two writes are atomic". Atomicity is a Postgres transaction
guarantee enforced inside the SECURITY DEFINER fn — out of vitest
scope.

Refs #3205.

* docs(legal): Art. 30 PA 11 + TC_VERSION bump-policy rubric

Article 30 register gains Processing Activity 11 — Consent Records
covering the new public.tc_acceptances ledger introduced by migration
044. Records lawful basis (Art. 6(1)(b) + Art. 7 demonstrability),

New knowledge-base/legal/tc-version-bump-policy.md provides the
3-tier rubric (material / clarifying / cosmetic) the CLO requires
for every T&C edit. Rubric:

    basis, new sub-processor, narrowed user rights, new retention,
    new jurisdiction, new subscription/refund terms, new EU
    consumer-rights provisions.
  - Tier 2 (clarifying): bump TC_VERSION (PATCH). Re-wording, re-
    numbering, splitting bullets, cross-reference fixes, examples.
  - Tier 3 (cosmetic): NO bump. Typo, whitespace, markdown-syntax
    fixes that don't change meaning. TC_DOCUMENT_SHA still updates.

"If unsure, treat as clarifying" — over-bumping is recoverable;
under-bumping leaks demonstrability.

Operator pre-flight checklist + CLO sign-off contract documented.

Refs #3205. AC15 + AC16 of the plan.

commit.message:
Change scope (#17)

* Add completed Rust verification proofs and standard h5i-app projects

* Record the verification campaign: certificates, evidence and Sol proofs

Independent certificates for 63 of the 103 selected specs, with the
harness that produces them (coverage, integration, project checks,
equivalence, performance, source inventory) and their raw evidence.

- run.py mounts codex-code-mode-host next to codex; codex >= 0.162 fails
  every tool call without it.
- nora glob_match_spec and transition_total gain a `< Usize.max` length
  precondition: gpt-6.1-sol proved both unconditional statements false
  (a pattern of Usize.max stars splits into more parts than a Vec holds).
  The counterexamples are kept under results/verification/.
- results/verification/spec-corrections.json lists every statement
  correction with its reason.

* Redesign the dashboard around verification coverage and runtime cost

The benchmark now asks how much real-world Rust h5i-app can verify and
what the port costs at runtime, not which model proves more. The page
reads the independent certificates instead of agent scores and shows,
per application, accepted specs, upstream lines reached by accepted
theorems, port and module scope, the extraction, differential-test and
project gates, paired kernel/upstream timings (matched boundaries apart
from unequal ones), and Lean-to-Rust effort. Spec details gain the
accepted proof and any statement correction.

Uses the h5i.dev palette and fonts with a terminal layout after
decbench.com, and a light theme. dashboard.py now finds upstream code
in plain (non-git) upstream copies and in repository-relative Source
paths written by `h5i app extract`.

* Shorten the dashboard headline

* Tighten the dashboard copy; refresh certificates and data

* nora middleware_total: require OIDC patterns shorter than Usize.max

gpt-6.1-sol proved the unconditional statement false through the OIDC
path (same capacity boundary as glob_match_spec); counterexample kept.

* Estimate each app's kernel ceiling and show coverage against it

harness/kernel_ceiling.py classifies every non-test function and data
item in the pinned upstream scope (a syn-based lister in
harness/kernel-ceiling/) as shell or kernel-eligible: shell items do
I/O, async, database, network, filesystem, clock, randomness,
environment, threads or locks, or are unsafe, or call such an item.
The eligible lines are the most an h5i-app kernel could hold. The
dashboard's verified table now shows reached lines over that ceiling
(3.7% overall, 1.9-14.1% per app) in place of ported/module lines.

* Count the security-relevant part of each kernel ceiling

Kernel-eligible items whose module path or name carries a security word
(auth, access, permission, token, credential, session, validation,
visibility, ...) form the security kernel: 70.5k of the 193.3k ceiling
lines. Accepted theorems reach 10.1% of it (5.8-37.3% per app); the
dashboard's verified table now shows this in place of the
selected-scope bar.

* Time path_clean with its String conversion; name every proof's prover

rustfs path_clean returned bytes on the kernel side but a String
upstream, so the timing left the shell's conversion out. The kernel
side now converts back with String::from_utf8_lossy, as upstream does:
0.86x instead of 0.72x. The remaining gap is the algorithm (an eager
copy instead of upstream's lazily copied buffer), now recorded in
DEVIATIONS.md, as is OxiCloud's match-based role table.

Proofs under ports/*/proofs/solutions/ were written by gpt-6.1-sol in
Codex sessions, and archived dashboard proofs carry their model in the
source; the dashboard shows these models instead of "proof session".

* Plot only matched-boundary timings; list the rest as excluded

Measurements whose upstream side includes HTTP request construction or
database round trips gave ratios like 0.02x that do not compare the
kernels. They are no longer plotted or offered as a filter; a collapsed
table lists them with the reason.

* Add a per-item port ledger; seed it for rustfs (1,182 of 2,538 target lines ported)

* Record new Sol certificates and refresh dashboard data (75 certificates)

* kanidm str_contains: bound the loop by subtraction; restore its spec

The port's str::contains looped while `i + needle.len() <= hay.len()`.
In Rust the sum cannot overflow, but in the extracted model a slice may
hold Usize.max bytes and it does: gpt-6.1-sol used this to prove
protected_deny_overrides_create false, and str_contains_spec needed a
length precondition. Looping while `i <= hay.len() - needle.len()`
computes the same result (difftest; a mutant fails) and removes the
overflow, so str_contains_spec is restored to its original statement
and the earlier certificate is kept as *-with-precondition.

Also: artifactkeeper repo_visibility_total bounds request byte strings
by Usize.max (a Cookie header of Usize.max `;` overflows split), with
the counterexample kept.

* Port rustfs built-in policies and complete action tables

* Give the dashboard h5i.dev's tab icon

* Port rustfs statement validation and resource set helpers

* rustfs bucket_policy_total: assume S3's bucket and key length limits

gpt-6.1-sol proved the unconditional statement false: a Usize.max-byte
bucket name overflows the resource ARN. Also: coverage.py rechecks the
previously accepted proof, and the kanidm anonymous-profile-only proof
from a run whose grading was interrupted is kept as a candidate.

* kanidm effective_permission_check_total: bound the profiles' attribute count

gpt-6.1-sol proved the unconditional statement false: Usize.max + 1
distinct granted attributes overflow the union of two search profiles.

* Port full condition metadata and binary and date operators

* Port Unicode claim lookup and decoded claim utilities

* Port complete condition key tables and server-derived predicates

* Port full rustfs policy metadata and management

* Port rustfs principal data and wildcard prefix helpers

* Port rustfs explicit-time policy document management

* Port complete rustfs variable context and claim resolution

* Record the overnight Sol certificates (94 of 103 accepted)

* rustfs: backport upstream's resolver-cycle fix; record two upstream findings

gpt-6.1-sol proved resolution_terminates false on the faithful port: at the
pinned e870a6d a pass rescans substituted text from offset 0 and can cycle
forever (an account named ${aws:username} hangs any policy that uses it).
The hang reproduces on the pinned upstream crate; rustfs fixed it in
03e77594 (2026-10-09). The kernel now carries that fix (Pending::resume,
depth limit 10), tested with upstream's regression cases and the proved
counterexample; a mutant that rescans from 0 fails them. The theorem
statement is unchanged; existing proofs still build. Randomized comparison
against the pinned crate still passes (36 tests).

results/verification/upstream-findings.json records this and OxiCloud's
non-monotonic role combination (MIN(role) ranks contributor above
commenter, but contributor lacks Comment).

* Re-certify rustfs specs against the fully ported, backported kernel; refresh dashboard data

* Bound the next field each totality counterexample used; resolver proof accepted

gpt-6.1-sol's latest counterexamples each used one more unbounded field,
so each statement gains only that bound (minimal assumptions):
nora namespace scopes, artifactkeeper query length (ticket decoding can
double it), kanidm sync-agreement attributes, rustfs condition key lookup
names, oxicloud membership rows, tuwunel relation rows. Counterexamples
are kept per spec. rustfs resolution_terminates is now proved for the
backported resolver (96 of 103 accepted).

* nora transition_total: also bound the request namespace (Sol's next counterexample)

* artifactkeeper repo_visibility_total: also bound total permission actions (Sol's next counterexample)

* kanidm effective_permission_check_total: reserve room for the 7 fixed attribute names

* oxicloud check_total: leave room for the user and the internal group

* rustfs bucket_policy_total: bound condition values and resource patterns by S3-sized limits

* tuwunel transition_total: bound relations by the recursive walker's queue, (n+1)^4

* kanidm effective_permission_check_total: reserve room for all 73 fixed names the modules insert

* Record rustfs var_name and compounding-substitution findings; keep partial totality proofs

* Move upstream findings out of this repo; neutral backport notes; re-certify rustfs

Upstream findings are tracked in a separate private repository. The rustfs
backport is described only by the upstream commit it follows, its tests
are upstream's own regression tests, and the 13 rustfs specs are
re-certified after the comment change (99 of 103 accepted).

* Drop the two specs blocked by upstream behavior; certificates hash only their own dataset entry

The selected set is now 101 specs (oxicloud fewer_grants_allow_no_more and
rustfs bucket_policy_total removed, with their property test and
evidence). Certificates previously hashed the whole dataset file, so any
dataset edit invalidated all of them; they now hash the task's own entry
(boundary v3, with a regression test), and all 99 accepted specs were
re-certified under it. 99 of 101 accepted.

  op:get touched the lock, so a holder demoted to Applicant could keep it

commit.message:
feat: username login, governance, asset, CMDB and operations modules (#51)

* feat(auth): sign in with a username when there is no email to invite

Staff without a corporate mailbox had no way into the system at all. The only
way to create an account was inviteUserByEmail, which needs a real inbox to
receive the link, so anyone without one simply could not be given access.

They now get an ordinary Supabase Auth account whose email is an internal
address on the reserved .invalid TLD that they never see or type. What they log
in with is the new profiles.username, and the login form takes either that or an
email in one field. Supabase Auth only accepts email or phone as an identifier,
so the page asks the Worker to translate what was typed before handing it to
signInWithPassword; the password check still happens against Supabase directly
from the browser, exactly as before. That lookup answers with the same shape
whether or not the account exists, returning a fixed unusable address when it
does not, so a failed sign-in cannot be used to work out which usernames are
real. It matches on equality through a SECURITY DEFINER function rather than a
PostgREST filter string, because a "%" typed into a filter built by hand would
match a real row and hand back a stranger's address.

The username is written by handle_new_user() in the same insert that creates the
profile. Writing it afterwards would leave an account nobody can reach if that
second write failed, and doing it together lets the unique index reject a taken
name before any auth user survives.

Suspending an account already worked end to end: the API bans the identity in
Supabase Auth and the middleware rechecks the profile status on every request,
so an issued JWT stops working immediately. Only the button was missing, so the
user list now has one, behind a confirmation that says what it does.

Admins can also set a password for someone. Username accounts have no inbox to
receive a reset link, so without this a forgotten password would strand them
permanently, and it helps email accounts locked out of their own mail too.

Three things turned up while building this. The login log validated its field as
an email, so every failed sign-in with a plain username would have been rejected
by the log endpoint and the attempt would have vanished from the audit trail.
my_profile() had to be dropped and recreated to widen its result, which quietly
reverts it to whatever the migration writes, and the onboarding columns a later
migration added would have been dropped along the way. handle_new_user() had
likewise been hardened to search_path = public, pg_temp after it was first
written, and a plain replace would have silently undone that.

Also lands the retirement of the public guest intake and the removal of the
legacy Apps Script tree, both already prepared in the working tree.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let the protected API and account deletion take a native app's bearer token, and check membership on it (#566)

* Pin that the protected API takes a native app's bearer token (wm-aj2eb, tests)

An app in a native shell holds no cookie for the instance, only the token
its sign-in handed back. Only GET /api/auth/me and the MCP and agent group
take that token today, so every read after sign-in is refused. These tests
fail against v3 for exactly that reason:

- serve: a token with no cookie reaches core's protected routes, a dynamic
  resource route and a preset handler mounted Protected, and a browser
  session still reaches every one of them; a token beside another person's
  cookie is answered for the token's person, and a bad token beside a good
  cookie is refused; DELETE /api/account takes the token alone, and a
  session as before; an account locked for deletion refuses its token with
  account_erasure_pending and still lets that token finish the deletion.
- wm-jwojd: a person removed from an account is refused on their token with
  account_access_revoked, on the protected routes and on the MCP group,
  which share the check; the refusal comes before the account's own state,
  as on the session path, and an unreadable membership fails closed.
- middleware: the deletion route's token path admits a locked account's
  token, marked, and refuses what the bearer path refuses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Let the protected API take a native app's bearer token, and check membership on it (wm-aj2eb, wm-jwojd)

An app in a native shell holds no cookie for the instance, only the token
its sign-in handed back, so after /api/auth/me every read it made was
refused.

The protected group now authenticates as the MCP and agent group does:
ErasureGuard with DeferToBearer, then BearerOrSession over RequireAuth, then
Impersonation and AuthorizeResource. A token wins over a cookie beside it,
and preset handlers mounted Protected inherit the stack. A request with no
token takes the session path exactly as before.

DELETE /api/account takes a token too, through BearerOrSessionForErasure:
no token goes to SessionAuthForErasure as before; a token takes the same
token path, with the one admission the session route makes, a token scoped
to an account whose erasure is unfinished, marked, so the deletion can run
again from the app.

The token path now checks that the token's person still belongs to the
token's account, as ValidateSession does for a session (wm-jwojd). A removed
member gets the session path's 401 account_access_revoked, before anything
about the account's own state; an unreadable membership fails closed with
503, as an unreadable account state already did. This reaches the MCP group
and /api/auth/me as well, which share the path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Refuse a connector's OAuth token on the protected API and the deletion (wm-8i8ln)

The protected group and DELETE /api/account took any token ValidateToken
accepted, so an access token a third-party connector got from /oauth/token
reached roles, invites, impersonation and the account deletion, not only the
MCP and agent routes the person agreed to connect. The native sign-in token
was the one meant for those routes.

- internal/oauth: both grants now issue the access token with the claim
  token_use=oauth; IssuedToConnector reads it back.
- api/middleware: a RefuseConnectorTokens option on BearerOrSession and
  BearerOrSessionForErasure. A marked token is refused with 403
  {"error":"insufficient_scope","code":"token_not_allowed"} and an
  insufficient_scope challenge. It is valid, so 401 invalid_token would only
  send a connector to refresh and retry.
- serve: the option is set on the protected group and the deletion route,
  not on the MCP/agent group or GET /api/auth/me. A token with no mark (a
  native sign-in's, including any issued before this change) is unaffected.

Test: TestServe_AConnectorsTokenIsRefusedOnTheAccountAPIButNotOnMCP gets a
token through /oauth/register, /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token: 200 on
/api/mcp, 403 on the protected routes and DELETE /api/account, for the
exchanged and the refreshed token; the door's and a password sign-in's
tokens answer 200. Before the fix the connector's token deleted the account.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Refuse the refresh grant for a person removed from the account (wm-mo1bp)

A removed member's access token is refused on every route with an
invalid_token challenge, so a conformant connector refreshes. The refresh
grant issued a new token for the stored account after reading only the agent
and its accounts, so the connector looped: refresh, refused, refresh.

The refresh grant now reads the person's role in the stored account first.
No role: the refresh token is revoked and the answer is 400 invalid_grant,
which ends the loop; the token stays refused if the person is added back, so
a new authorization is the way in. A membership that cannot be read answers
500 server_error, issues nothing and revokes nothing.

Tests: TestServe_TheRefreshGrantRefusesAPersonRemovedFromTheAccount connects
a client through serve's own /oauth routes, removes the person, and gets
invalid_grant, then invalid_grant again after the membership is restored.
Before the fix the refresh answered 200. TestTokenHandler_RefreshToken_
ChecksTheMembership covers a member (whose refreshed token carries the
connector mark), a removed person (revoked) and an unreadable membership.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Hand a locked account's owner a sign-in token, so the app can finish the deletion (wm-xsvas)

The deletion route admits a token scoped to an account whose erasure began
and did not finish, but sign-in refused to issue any token for such an
account. An app in a native shell holds no cookie, so once its original token
expired it could never finish a deletion that failed part-way.

Sign-in now issues the token for the locked account whenever it scopes the
session to it, which is only for the account's owner or admin
(LockedAccountFor). A plain member of a locked account, or an owner of a
merely suspended one, still signs in unscoped and gets no token. The token
is refused with account_erasure_pending on every route except
DELETE /api/account. The stale comment that said a locked account's token
could serve nothing is rewritten.

Test: TestServe_ASignInToALockedAccountHandsBackATokenForTheDeletionOnly,
for password sign-in and the door: sign in, lock and deactivate the account,
sign in again. The answer names the locked account with
account_erasure_pending and a token; the token gets 401
account_erasure_pending on /api/resource-types, a preset handler,
/api/auth/me and /api/mcp, and 200 on DELETE /api/account. Before the fix
the sign-in carried no token. The handler tests pin the token for an owner
and no token for a plain member or a suspended account.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Refuse a bearer token that names no account with unscoped_session (wm-92vba)

The token path checked the account, the membership and the account state only
when the token named an account. A valid token that named none was admitted
with an identity that named no account, and since wm-aj2eb that reached every
protected route, not only the MCP and agent group. The session path refuses
that shape with 401 unscoped_session.

The token path now refuses it the same way, right after the signature check:
401 {"error":"not authenticated","code":"unscoped_session"}, with the
invalid_token challenge a refused token carries. It applies to every group
that takes a token: the protected API, MCP and agent, the deletion route and
GET /api/auth/me. No sign-in issues such a token today; this closes the path
for any issuer that ever does.

Tests: TestServe_ATokenThatNamesNoAccountIsRefusedAsAnUnscopedSessionIs mints
one with serve's own JWT service: 401 unscoped_session on
/api/resource-types, a preset handler, DELETE /api/account and /api/mcp.
Before the fix three answered 200 and the deletion answered a bare 401.
TestBearerOrSession_RefusesATokenThatNamesNoAccount pins the body and the
challenge on BearerOrSession and BearerOrSessionForErasure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Say account_gone when a token's account no longer exists (wm-sx2zx)

A token whose account was deleted was refused with a bare 401 invalid_token,
the same answer an expired token gets. An app that had just finished an
in-app deletion took its next background call's refusal as an expired
session and offered to sign in again, to an account that is gone.

The bearer path now answers a gone account with
{"error":"invalid_token","code":"account_gone"}. It keeps the 401 and the
invalid_token challenge, so a client that reads only the status or the
challenge sees no change. The code is additive; the session path is
unchanged.

Tests: TestServe_TheAccountDeletionAnswersTheTokenAlone deletes the account
with its token, then asserts 401 account_gone with the invalid_token
challenge for that token. Before the fix the body carried no code. The
middleware "gone" cases (BearerOrSession and BearerOrSessionForErasure) and
the identity read's gone-account case now expect account_gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Say when to retry an account-state 503, and name the membership index (wm-w0bha)

The token path fails closed with 503 when it cannot read the token's
account or the person's membership, and it gave no Retry-After, so an agent
client read a database blip as an outage.

Every "could not read the account's state" 503 in the auth middleware now
carries Retry-After: 5 (the token path's account and membership reads,
ErasureGuard's lock read, and SessionAuthForErasure's lock read). All three
go through one answer; the body and the status are unchanged.

The membership read is an indexed point read. FindMemberRole's query is
SELECT * FROM account_members WHERE account_id = ? AND agent_id = ?
ORDER BY account_id LIMIT 1. The table's primary key is
(account_id, agent_id), and on SQLite the plan is SEARCH account_members
USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_account_members_1 (account_id=? AND
agent_id=?); on Postgres the same key is account_members_pkey. A bearer
request makes two primary-key reads (accounts by id, then the membership),
plus the erasure lock read only when the account is inactive. No cache.

Tests: the fail-closed tests for an unreadable membership, account, and
lock (token path, ErasureGuard, SessionAuthForErasure) now require the
Retry-After header. They failed before the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Revert "Say account_gone when a token's account no longer exists (wm-sx2zx)"

This reverts commit 34e695f2.

The change contradicts a merged acceptance scenario.
tests/e2e/features/account_deletion.feature:402, "The identity read with an
app's sign-in token is refused after the deletion", ends with "And the
refusal carries no code". That step was added by a3f85f73 (#565). With
account_gone, TestAccountDeletion fails on that scenario.

Changing an acceptance contract, or answering the identity read differently
from the other routes to get around it, is not this fix's decision. The
refusal for a gone account stays a bare 401 invalid_token until the
contract is decided. 34e695f2 holds the ready implementation and its tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Check the membership again when a connector exchanges its code (wm-aj2eb)

Copilot review on #566, point 1: the authorization-code grant issued a
connector access/refresh pair without rechecking that the person still
belongs to the account they authorized. A person removed between
authorizing and the exchange still got a refresh token, which could mint
access again after a later re-add with no new authorization.

The grant now reads FindMemberRole for (AccountID, AgentID) once the code
is claimed: no role answers invalid_grant and keeps no refresh token, and
a membership that cannot be read answers server_error, matching the
refresh grant (wm-mo1bp).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Refuse a removed member's refresh only once the token is revoked (wm-aj2eb)

Copilot review on #566, point 2: when a removed member refreshed, a failed
Revoke was only logged and the grant still answered invalid_grant. The
refresh token stayed live, so it could mint a connector token again after
the person was added back, despite the revocation the refusal promised.

A revocation that cannot be written now answers server_error, so the
client retries and the revocation is tried again; invalid_grant is sent
only after the token is revoked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xr4BbcFgXUnuxHHDvjVbjN

* Refuse a connector's token before the account's state (wm-aj2eb)

Copilot review 5203391068, point 1: on a group that passed
RefuseConnectorTokens, a connector's token for a suspended account, or for
an erasure-locked account on the protected group, was answered 401
invalid_token account_deactivated / account_erasure_pending, because the
connector refusal ran after the account-state switch. A connector told
invalid_token refreshes and tries again, and the refresh grant does not
read the account's state, so it could loop for a token no refresh makes
acceptable on this route.

The refusal now runs after the account is found and the membership is
confirmed, and before the state switch: 403 insufficient_scope
token_not_allowed in every state. A gone account and a removed member keep
their own 401s, an unreadable state or membership still fails closed with
503 and Retry-After, native tokens keep every answer they had, and a locked
account's owner still reaches the deletion with a native token only.

commit.message:
feat(auth): add instance access role member (#1598)

* feat(auth): add instance access role member

Consume instance access role `member` as owner minus member management.
Unknown HTTP APIs fail closed to member; allowlist mutation stays owner-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): honor member on advertised project and agent management

Lower project CRUD and Organization Agent onboarding from owner identity to
the can_manage_* rank so a remote member can actually use the surfaces the
capability projection advertises. Seed every existing role in the tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): register agent ACL for personal member create

Drop the organization-membership gate on VibeAgentStore.create so a
Personal/email member who can_manage_agents gets a private policy row.
Missing-policy fails closed for non-owners, which hid the Agent from
its creator. Organization use still follows the stored ACL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): keep remote-access pairing identity owner-only

Default /api/remote-access writes to owner so a newly added pair/unpair
sibling cannot slip through as member. Member keeps the read/ops routes
that cannot change instance id, backend URL, or secrets. Pair itself
re-checks can_manage_access_members, and POST /api/config strips the
whole vibe_cloud section for non-owners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): keep pairing identity and default-agent owner-only

Non-owner POST /api/config now drops the entire remote_access key, so
falsy or non-object patches cannot wipe pairing identity. Instance-wide
default-agent mutation stays owner-only at both the HTTP rule and setter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): require default routing Agents to be audience-usable

Default routing surfaces -- the instance-wide default Agent and a
project's default Agent -- are resolved on behalf of whoever starts an
unpinned session, never on behalf of whoever configured them. So the
invariant both share: a default must reference an Agent usable by the
audience it routes for.

update_project persisted a project default on DB existence alone, so a
member could pin their private-policy Agent as a shared project's
default; every other project user then failed
ensure_agent_selection_access on the unpinned create_session path and the
project could no longer start normal sessions.

Add one shared predicate, default_routing_audience_error, and call it
from both surfaces. A private ACL is single-subject by construction, so
it is refused; an Agent with no ACL row is the local/builtin shape and is
unaffected. The check is caller-independent: the Owner's ACL bypass
describes the Owner, not the audience a default must serve.

create_project accepts no default-Agent field, so update_project is the
only project entry point.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): require default routing Agents to be audience-wide

The shared default-routing predicate rejected only the `private` shape, so a
`scope` policy still passed: a member could publish an Agent to group A and set
it as the default of a project whose audience includes group B, and everyone
outside A then failed `ensure_agent_selection_access` on the unpinned path --
the same break the private case caused, through a different access level.

Close the class instead of the variant. The invariant is stated positively in
the predicate: a default must be usable by its entire audience, so only an
audience-wide policy qualifies. `AUDIENCE_WIDE_ACCESS_LEVELS` lists what does
qualify rather than what does not, so an access level added later is rejected
until it is deliberately declared audience-wide.

Group-subset comparison is intentionally not implemented. A project is not an
ACL resource kind and carries no group binding, so a project audience is not
representable, and an instance-wide default has no bounded audience to compare
against at all -- defaults do not get narrower audiences.

The error codes are renamed to match the widened rule
(`agent_default_audience_restricted`, `project_agent_audience_restricted`);
both surfaces keep their established HTTP shapes, a coded 400 for the project
default and 403 `agent_access_forbidden` for the instance-wide one.

Tests derive the restricted set from `ACCESS_LEVELS - AUDIENCE_WIDE_ACCESS_LEVELS`
rather than listing it, so a new access level is covered without editing them.
Legacy databases can still hold a scoped instance default, which the setter no
longer produces, so those read paths are now seeded directly and asserted to
keep resolving for a caller inside the scope.

* test(auth): drop the retired show_page kind from the member route list

Rebase adaptation. Master retired the show_page resource ACL (36dabbee), so
`show_page` is no longer a member of `resource_access_service.RESOURCE_KINDS`
and naming it in the member-reachable route example asserts against a kind that
no longer exists. The route pattern is kind-agnostic, so the assertion still
passed while documenting a dead shape.

Use `agent`, matching the kind master's own permissions tests moved to. The
member-role semantics under test are unchanged: this route stays reachable at
`member`.

* fix(auth): keep instance access administration owner-only

The member set an Instance Owner controls is cloud allowlist entries AND
multi-platform IM bound users, not the allowlist alone: a principal reaches
this instance just as directly by being a bound IM user, an IM admin unlocks
protected setup/routing/update actions, and a bind code is a bearer credential
that mints exactly that access. Gate /api/users mutations, /api/bind-codes
CRUD, and GET /api/setup/first-bind-code at the route policy table and in the
handlers. GET /api/users stays at member -- it discloses the member set without
disclosing a credential, matching the cloud allowlist whose GET is member and
whose PUT is Owner.

Bulk Agent onboarding (GET and POST /api/agent-onboarding) becomes Owner-only
for a different reason: it is an instance-wide one-way migration whose GET
discloses every Agent row and whose POST claims every policy-less Agent under
the caller's private ACL. It is deliberately not gated on
can_manage_access_members, because a migration tool is not member management.

Both surfaces are swept from the live router rather than from a list of known
routes, so a bind-code, bound-user, or onboarding sibling added later fails the
test until it is classified, and a second test drives the handlers with the
policy table disarmed so each layer is proven on its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): default unclassified API routes to owner and enforce agent ACL at use time

Two review classes closed at their root instead of one route or one
predicate at a time.

Class 1 -- the member rank silently widened 112 routes. The unknown
`/api/*` fallback in `http_authorization_policy` had been changed from
`owner` to `member`, so every route nobody had classified became
member-reachable: `POST /api/control`, `POST /api/upgrade`, every
`/api/backend/*/auth`, `POST /api/logs`, both permissions ACL writes,
`POST /api/settings`. Enumerating exceptions could not converge, because
the set grows with every new route. Invert it: the fallback returns
`owner` again, and the member-reachable surface is one explicit
declaration (`_MEMBER_HTTP_RULES`) grouped by namespace and method.
Member drops 116 -> 28 routes, owner rises 15 -> 103. A property test
sweeps the live router and asserts every registered `/api/*` route
resolves to an explicit tier, and that a route nobody has classified --
including one that does not exist yet -- resolves to `owner`.

Class 2 -- validating a default Agent's ACL *shape* at bind time is
unclosable. No predicate over {public, scope, private, absent} is both
sound and usable: `private` and `scope` narrow the audience, `absent` is
the normal shape on a personal install where no Agent carries an ACL row
at all, and `public` still admits only active members of the policy's
organization while instance and project access are also granted to email
and email-domain principals. So a default is advisory, and the ACL is
enforced where it is meaningful: at use time, against the principal
actually resolving it. `resolve_usable_default_agent` degrades an
unusable default to a builtin, then to any other enabled Agent the caller
may use, and returns the existing machine-readable access error only when
nothing is usable. `create_session` routes an inherited project default
through the same path rather than the hard-erroring selection gate.
`set_default_agent_name` keeps its owner-only gate; explicit Agent
selection is a stated intent and still errors.

The project-access editor is re-gated on `can_manage_access_members`,
matching the now-owner-only ACL write behind it.

Evidence: unit (tests/test_instance_authorization.py,
tests/test_permissions.py, tests/test_resource_acl_agents.py,
tests/test_projects_service.py, PermissionsPage.test.tsx), router-sweep
property test, ruff, ui build.

Wires the two closures that already landed into the paths that actually run.

resolve_usable_default_agent answers a question about one principal, so
create_session throwing the answer away made the degradation a no-op: dispatch
re-derived the route from Controller.resolve_vibe_agent_for_context, which
carries no principal, pinned the inaccessible configured default, and the
execution-time recheck retired the caller's first message. Persist the
substitute onto the session when (and only when) the default actually degraded,
so _delivery_backend_in_transaction satisfies itself from the durable binding.
Explicit selection is unchanged and still fails closed.

Project mutations checked the instance role only, which answers whether a
principal administers Projects at all, not which ones. list_projects and
get_project already hid restricted Projects a member is excluded from, so a
member who knew an id could PATCH or archive one. update_project and
archive_project now go through the same can_read_project the list path uses,
and the HTTP middleware applies the ACL's visibility floor to member-tier
routes instead of skipping them. Personal installs are unaffected:
get_effective_project_role short-circuits there.

Evidence: unit + HTTP route tests; both new locks fail on the prior head.

* fix(auth): gate project lookups and non-owner config writes as whole graphs

Two invariants, each closed at its resolver rather than at the call sites
that happen to exist today:

   now takes the authorization context and refuses a match the caller cannot

member allow-list while the policy comment directly above that table
already declared dependency installs Owner-only. The handler runs a
package manager, a self-update, or a curl script on the host, persists
the resulting CLI path, and may restart the backend -- host lifecycle,
not the Agent CRUD the member rank is defined to grant.

before the member rank existed, so absence is the enforcement and no
second regex table has to stay in sync.

declared on the member allow-list, and viewer/editor/member all get 403

stubbed, and the test ends by asserting only the owner leg ever reached
the handler, so no package manager runs.
