commit.message:
Split indicator editing into versions (#129)

* Analyse the seed tables after loading them

A freshly loaded table carries no statistics, so the planner falls back
to fixed guesses and picks a sequential scan over the whole observation
table where an index scan is available. The read-model rebuild already
analyses what it writes; the seed now does the same for the tables it
loads and the memberships the relationship import writes.

* Split indicator editing into versions

An indicator becomes an identity row — id, short id, when its data was
last published — and everything a publisher edits moves to
indicator_version, one row per draft or publication. The metadata table
folds into the version and topic and classification memberships attach
to it, so a draft can be edited without touching what the public sees.
Partial unique indexes make "one draft" and "one published version per
indicator" constraints rather than convention.

public_api loses every table grant. It gets USAGE on a new published
schema and SELECT on the views in it, and every predicate that keeps an
unpublished indicator out of the public site now lives in a view
definition instead of in each query. internal_api reads the views too,
since it mounts the public routes, and gains the writes on the indicator
tables the create-indicator stories need.

Nothing is migrated in place: the seed files are reshaped and every
environment is reset and reseeded. status, supersedes_id, reviewed_at
and reviewed_by go, and the internal side derives an indicator's status
from its versions — draft while one exists, published otherwise.

* Pin what the public role may reach

A throwaway member of public_api inherits the public grants without
bootstrapping or renaming the cluster-wide role, so the test can ask the
catalog directly: no privilege of any kind on any relation in public,
SELECT and nothing else on every view in published. Connected as that
role, an indicator whose only version is a draft — with observations,
bridge rows and read-model rows behind it — returns nothing through any
of the views.

This runs against every future migration, so a table granted to
public_api by mistake fails here rather than reaching the public site.

* Document the published schema and the reshaped seed

The "adding a table" checklist gains the view and the grant on the view,
which is now how a table reaches the public site. The seed notes record
that every indicator loads as a single published version and that
reshaping the Pholio export is a step in regenerating the snapshot.

* Fix what the e2e run found in the version split

Two defects the unit and integration tiers missed.

greatest() over the version timestamps came back as the driver's string,
so the dashboard's JSON serialisation threw; mapWith gives the fragment
the column's decoder. Drizzle keys its column-name cache on the
unqualified relation name, so on internal-api — which reads the indicator
table and the published indicator view from one connection — whichever
was queried first decided the other's columns, and the public facets and
search routes failed. Spelling the view columns' names out skips the
cache altogether.

The internal integration tests now cover both: a Date on the dashboard
row, and the two surfaces queried in one process. The overview spec
matches the status tag exactly, since "Published" is also in the link
below it.

* Export the published snapshot in the version shape

export-published-snapshot.py emits an identity indicator row and one
published indicator_version row per approved source indicator, so a
fresh archive matches SEED_TABLES after the split. The deterministic
transform reads that shape, strip-metadata-html.py finds the prose in
whichever file the export produced, and the export now fails before
streaming 29 million rows if a source indicator records no actor:
indicator_version.created_by and updated_by are NOT NULL.

* Check the imported snapshot's version status

indicator no longer carries a status, so the recheck inside the import
transaction looks for a version that is not published. Verification
also requires the manifest to hold one published version per approved
indicator.

* Require a name on every indicator version

A draft is only ever created from the page that asks for a name, so a
version without one has no reason to exist. Migration 0015 is unreleased
and this branch owns it, so the NOT NULL goes into its CREATE TABLE
rather than into a new migration.

createIndicatorDraft takes NewIndicatorDraftAttributes, which requires
the name. An update still rewrites only the columns it names, and can no
longer clear it.

* Let an indicator keep several published versions

Superseded-version statuses come with later work, so the only status
constraint now is one draft per indicator. Reads mean the most recently
published version by that: among an indicator's published rows, order by
published_at descending with nulls last, then by id, which is UUIDv7 and
so orders by creation.

The published views apply that rule, and latestPublishedVersion applies
it to queries over the tables, so the membership views, the dashboard's
derived name and date, the seed's topic links and a draft opened from
what is published all follow the same version.

* Reject a snapshot whose versions are not one per indicator

* Add slugify to the shared slug rule

An indicator's public address is derived from its name, so the rule that
derives it belongs beside SLUG_PATTERN in @fphd/config/slug, where the
database schemas, the wire contracts and the web apps can all reach it
without taking a Node dependency.

slugProblem names the three ways a name yields no usable slug:
nothing left, digits only, or a reserved route segment. The name page
turns each into its own message.

* Add a slug to every indicator version

The public address of an indicator is its name, slugified. The column is
NOT NULL because every version is named, and an exclusion constraint,
which drizzle cannot express, keeps a slug to one indicator for ever:
versions of one indicator may share it, two indicators may not, and a
draft holds its slug until it is deleted.

published.indicator gains the canonical slug — the latest published
version's — and published.indicator_slug lists every slug a published
version carries, so an address an indicator has outgrown still resolves
without the public role reading the version table.

* Derive seed slugs in the export pipeline

Seed rows arrive by COPY, so the CSV has to carry the slug the app would
have derived. slug.py mirrors @fphd/config/slug; where two names
slugify alike the lower short id keeps the bare slug and the other takes
its number. A name yielding nothing usable stops the export rather than
being worked around.

A TypeScript test reads the committed CSV and checks every slug against
the TypeScript rule, so the two implementations cannot drift.

The hosted published-snapshot archive gains the column from
add-version-slugs.py; until it is regenerated the importer refuses it by
name rather than failing inside the COPY.

* Slug a draft from its name on every write

createIndicatorDraft, updateIndicatorDraft and createDraftFromPublished
derive the slug rather than taking one, so the column can never disagree
with the name. A name whose slug another indicator holds comes back as
{ ok: false, reason: 'slug_taken' } for the name page to show as a field
error; a name that yields no slug at all throws, because the page
refuses those before they reach here.

Published versions are never written by these functions, so their slugs
are immutable by construction. The indicator overview links to the
published slug, and so has no action while nothing is published.

* Serve an indicator by slug or short id

/api/indicators/:indicator and its data and range routes resolve a
digits-only segment as a short id and anything else as a slug,
lower-cased, and answer 200 either way: a stored address keeps working
rather than being redirected, and choosing a canonical one is the web
app's job. Detail, list and search bodies carry the canonical slug
alongside the short id.

Search's exact-identifier match now covers a slug-shaped query as well
as a digit string, case-folded, against every published slug. A short id
too large for the column is a 404 rather than a query that errors.

* Address indicator pages by slug

indicators/:slug replaces indicators/:shortId in both apps, downloads
included. The loader hands the segment to the API as it stands and,
when the canonical slug differs (a number, an older slug, the wrong
case), answers 301 to it with the query string intact. Links
in search results and on the dashboard are built from the slug; the
compare selection stays short ids, which is what it addresses.

The page indicator's detail is fetched once and reused for the selection
rather than being fetched again alongside the compared ones.

* Expect the published indicator to open by slug

* Answer the slug review comments

The search test now exercises searchIndicators, a digit run longer than a short id is refused before the API is asked, the seed README says which pipeline reshapes, and the overview comment matches the check it sits on.

* Say published, not approved, on the public read surface

The public repositories read the published views, so their names now say so. The Pholio export and the snapshot manifest keep the source system's approved status.

* Sort the renamed exports

* Bound a short-id segment by the column, not its digits

Ten digits is not the same limit as a Postgres integer, so
isIndicatorSegment still forwarded 9999999999 to the API. The rule now
lives once in @fphd/config/short-id, beside the slug rule and with no
server dependency, and the route check, the API's identifier resolution
and search's exact match all read it.

* Refuse a reserved word as an indicator segment

A reserved word names an API collection endpoint, so the page
loader was calling it and failing to read the answer. The route
now answers 404 without asking the API.

* Give a slug room for a whole name and refuse collisions

The limit rises from 80 to 200 characters: Fingertips names run to about
180, and cutting shorter made names that differ only in their tail share
a slug. With that gone, the export no longer suffixes a colliding slug
with the short id; it stops before writing anything, naming the pairs.

Four approved indicators share a name with a newer indicator and are
left out of the published snapshot with their data. The importer holds
the same list and refuses an archive built with another. The dummy seed
drops the one of those it held, so it holds 12 indicators, and its three
truncated slugs are re-derived.

* Define the published version once and keep its slug

current_published_version is a view in public: the most recently
published version of each indicator, ties broken by id. The published
views join it in place of three copies of the DISTINCT ON, and the
internal reads join it in place of a QueryBuilder subquery. A check ties
published_at to the status, so the ordering never meets a null.

A draft opened from a published version copies its slug, and a rename
re-slugs a draft only while nothing is published: once an indicator has
a public address, every version keeps it. The seed's topic import
attaches memberships to the published version where there is one and to
the draft otherwise, so a draft-only indicator takes its links and its
data timestamp rather than being reported unknown.

* Redirect a superseded slug temporarily and drop the slug backfill

A number or a case variant has one permanent home, so it still 301s. A
superseded slug answers 302: versions of one indicator share a slug, so
an old address could become canonical again, and a browser holding a
cached 301 each way would loop between them.

Migration 0017 adds the slug column NOT NULL directly. Nothing migrates
a populated database, so the placeholder backfill had nothing to fill.

* Treat a dash or a slash as a word separator in a slug

Dropped, they ran words together: "palliative/supportive" became
"palliativesupportive", "and/or" became "andor" and an en-dashed "0–4"
became "04". Mapped to a hyphen like whitespace, 53 of the approved
Fingertips names read as written, and none collide. No committed seed
slug changes.

* Count the twelve seeded indicators in the search specs

* Verify the exclusions exactly, check every name, redirect before fetching

The export records how many observations the excluded indicators
carried, and the importer requires the archive to hold the source total
less that number rather than merely fewer.

A rename of a published indicator keeps its slug but the name is still
checked, so an unusable one is refused rather than written.

A download addressed by number or by an old slug is redirected before
its data is asked for, so an unknown area no longer turns the redirect
into a 404.

* Compare the exclusion lists as sets

* Squash the four version migrations into one

drizzle-kit generates the table, the column drops, the indexes, the checks
and current_published_version; the exclusion constraint, the published
views and the grants follow by hand in their final form, so the rule for
the published version is written once rather than four times and replaced.
The two ADD COLUMN statements are moved ahead of the primary keys that
name them, which drizzle-kit emitted in the wrong order.

* Enforce the slug shape in the database

indicator_version.slug was held only by the exclusion constraint, so a
write that bypassed slugify could store a slug no route would resolve.
A CHECK now requires the shared pattern, refuses digits only (which
would read as a short id) and caps the length at SLUG_MAX_LENGTH.
Reserved words stay an application rule. The schema builds the pattern
and the limit from @fphd/config/slug, so changing either shows up as a
schema change. Migration 0015 is edited in place, as the branch is
unmerged.

* Spell out the whitespace a slug splits on

`\s` means different things in JavaScript and Python: JavaScript counts
U+FEFF, Python counts U+0085 and U+001C-001F. slugify and the seed
export's copy of it could therefore derive different slugs from one
name. Both now use the same explicit class, Unicode White_Space plus
the dashes and slashes, so U+FEFF and the information separators are
dropped and U+0085 separates words in both.

* Refuse an export missing a foreign-key column

The UUID transform skipped any foreign-key column a file did not carry,
so an export that lost one would keep its integer keys unnoticed. Only
the published export's indicator file, which holds identity columns
alone, may lack them; any other table missing one now stops the
transform.

* Bring the seed export and counts in line

The export list carried 93283, which the committed seed does not hold,
so a re-export would not reproduce it. The list is back to the nine
Pholio indicators in the seed, and the READMEs and a comment that still
counted 13 or the original ten now match the 12 seeded indicators.

* Name the internal role test for what it checks

internal_api now writes the indicator, version, membership and topic
tables, so it no longer connects with a read-only role. The test only
asserts that it cannot write reference data, and is named for that.

* Keep _routes out of canonical redirects

A client-side navigation fetches the page's data with React Router's
_routes parameter, and the slug redirects copied the whole query
string, so the canonical address they sent the browser to carried it
too. pageSearch returns the query as the page sees it, without
_routes. The indicator and CSV redirects use it, and so does the
session middleware, which already stripped the parameter itself.

* Refuse an indicator export missing only some foreign keys

The identity-only published export lacks every indicator foreign-key
column. A regular export lacking just some of them is malformed, and
is now refused rather than rekeyed with those columns left alone.

* Define the published version once and keep its slug

current_published_version is a view in public: the most recently
published version of each indicator, ties broken by id. The published
views join it in place of three copies of the DISTINCT ON, and the
internal reads join it in place of a QueryBuilder subquery. A check ties
published_at to the status, so the ordering never meets a null.

A draft opened from a published version copies its slug, and a rename
re-slugs a draft only while nothing is published: once an indicator has
a public address, every version keeps it. The seed's topic import
attaches memberships to the published version where there is one and to
the draft otherwise, so a draft-only indicator takes its links and its
data timestamp rather than being reported unknown.

* Redirect a superseded slug temporarily and drop the slug backfill

A number or a case variant has one permanent home, so it still 301s. A
superseded slug answers 302: versions of one indicator share a slug, so
an old address could become canonical again, and a browser holding a
cached 301 each way would loop between them.

Migration 0017 adds the slug column NOT NULL directly. Nothing migrates
a populated database, so the placeholder backfill had nothing to fill.

* Treat a dash or a slash as a word separator in a slug

Dropped, they ran words together: "palliative/supportive" became
"palliativesupportive", "and/or" became "andor" and an en-dashed "0–4"
became "04". Mapped to a hyphen like whitespace, 53 of the approved
Fingertips names read as written, and none collide. No committed seed
slug changes.

* Count the twelve seeded indicators in the search specs

* Verify the exclusions exactly, check every name, redirect before fetching

The export records how many observations the excluded indicators
carried, and the importer requires the archive to hold the source total
less that number rather than merely fewer.

A rename of a published indicator keeps its slug but the name is still
checked, so an unusable one is refused rather than written.

A download addressed by number or by an old slug is redirected before
its data is asked for, so an unknown area no longer turns the redirect
into a 404.

* Compare the exclusion lists as sets

* Squash the four version migrations into one

drizzle-kit generates the table, the column drops, the indexes, the checks
and current_published_version; the exclusion constraint, the published
views and the grants follow by hand in their final form, so the rule for
the published version is written once rather than four times and replaced.
The two ADD COLUMN statements are moved ahead of the primary keys that
name them, which drizzle-kit emitted in the wrong order.

* Enforce the slug shape in the database

indicator_version.slug was held only by the exclusion constraint, so a
write that bypassed slugify could store a slug no route would resolve.
A CHECK now requires the shared pattern, refuses digits only (which
would read as a short id) and caps the length at SLUG_MAX_LENGTH.
Reserved words stay an application rule. The schema builds the pattern
and the limit from @fphd/config/slug, so changing either shows up as a
schema change. Migration 0015 is edited in place, as the branch is
unmerged.

* Spell out the whitespace a slug splits on

`\s` means different things in JavaScript and Python: JavaScript counts
U+FEFF, Python counts U+0085 and U+001C-001F. slugify and the seed
export's copy of it could therefore derive different slugs from one
name. Both now use the same explicit class, Unicode White_Space plus
the dashes and slashes, so U+FEFF and the information separators are
dropped and U+0085 separates words in both.

* Refuse an export missing a foreign-key column

The UUID transform skipped any foreign-key column a file did not carry,
so an export that lost one would keep its integer keys unnoticed. Only
the published export's indicator file, which holds identity columns
alone, may lack them; any other table missing one now stops the
transform.

* Bring the seed export and counts in line

The export list carried 93283, which the committed seed does not hold,
so a re-export would not reproduce it. The list is back to the nine
Pholio indicators in the seed, and the READMEs and a comment that still
counted 13 or the original ten now match the 12 seeded indicators.

* Name the internal role test for what it checks

internal_api now writes the indicator, version, membership and topic
tables, so it no longer connects with a read-only role. The test only
asserts that it cannot write reference data, and is named for that.

* Keep _routes out of canonical redirects

A client-side navigation fetches the page's data with React Router's
_routes parameter, and the slug redirects copied the whole query
string, so the canonical address they sent the browser to carried it
too. pageSearch returns the query as the page sees it, without
_routes. The indicator and CSV redirects use it, and so does the
session middleware, which already stripped the parameter itself.

* Refuse an indicator export missing only some foreign keys

The identity-only published export lacks every indicator foreign-key
column. A regular export lacking just some of them is malformed, and
is now refused rather than rekeyed with those columns left alone.

feat!: enforce code access for runs and results (#1871)

* feat: enforce code access

Require code access as well as model access to launch runs and read their
outputs through the API, warehouse RLS, monitoring, approvals and the relay.
Rebuilt on the S3 Object Lambda reader's removal, so the access point no longer
needs its own code check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(eval-log-reader): decide code access in the database

The S3 Object Lambda reader is a temporary bridge until it is deprecated:
after main's model check, it asks public.code_policy_has_access for the
key's own run, first with no code groups (so public code needs no Identity
Store lookups), then with the caller's code-access groups. An unreadable
policy or identity answers 503 rather than a deny. There is no admin or
owner exception.

The reader logs in as inspect-log-reader, which infra and the migration
limit to EXECUTE on that one function; check_rls_health restores the grant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(api): say which sources stopped a launch

A launch refused for an incomplete inventory now names each problem by
config location: the parser's redacted refusal reason, an unsupported Git
host, installer settings that can change sources, the source cap, a busy
parser or a timeout. Unexpected parser failures say only "could not be
identified". Raw sources and environment values never appear.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: describe the S3 reader's code check

The S3 Object Lambda reader is a temporary bridge: it asks the database's
code policy directly, with no admin or owner exception, and answers 503 when
it cannot decide. Admin bypass applies to API reads only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): answer busy or slow source checks with 503

A launch refused only because parsing was busy or timed out is not a
permission decision, and nothing is written yet; it now gets a 503 with the
same per-source list. A permanent problem alongside it keeps the 403.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(relay): report authorization outages as 503

When the API can't answer the access check (no response or a 5xx), attach
stays blocked but is refused with 503, not 403, so callers can tell an outage
from missing permission.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): serve usage without a database

Usage comes from CloudWatch; without a database no code check can run, so
job and task labels are hidden, as when the check fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): hide code-restricted sources when resolving transcripts

A scan by transcript id refuses ids in eval sets the caller can't access by

imports already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): require code access before issuing S3 credentials

The broker checked only model groups, so under enforcement a caller with
model access but no code grant could get credentials for a code-restricted
run, and a scan could read code-restricted sources. It now asks
public.code_policy_has_access, as the same narrow login as the S3 reader, for
any caller other than the run's own verified job and for every scan source.
An unanswerable check is a 503. The broker deploys after the migration that
creates the function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): keep readers when an unchanged resume is rejected

A resume rewrote its config even when unchanged, which counts as a source
write: if a later check (e.g. the outstanding-job limit) rejected it, the
inventory stayed pending and ordinary readers lost access. Under the launch
lock, an identical saved config is no longer rewritten, so a rejection
restores the previous inventory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): keep code grants in public-models-only mode

Public-only reduces a caller's model grants; it stripped code-access grants
too, so a scan over code-restricted sources got 403 from the broker even
for its own verified job.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): rewrite the config when the saved one can't be read

Any failure reading the saved config (malformed YAML, a connection error)
now means "not proven unchanged", so the resume writes the config as before
instead of failing with 500, which blocked repairing an unreadable config.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: check code access once per list, not once per row

Non-admin lists called a SECURITY DEFINER code check per row. PostgreSQL
can't inline those and re-plans every nested SQL function call, so the
viewer's eval-set list took 16 s at 52k eval sets (admin: 0.07 s).

- Lists (eval sets, jobs, scans, samples, usage labels) ask new set-based
  code_denied_* helpers once per query, like the model check's denied_*
  helpers. Samples narrow candidates to the query's own eval filters.
- Every function inlines one copy of the decision SQL instead of calling
  helpers; the owner waiver, scan sources and name rules are unchanged.
- RLS binds the reader's code groups once per statement. The wrapper now
  takes them as an argument and checks the role holds each one.
- Migration 6a91b42d08ef is edited in place: it has not run anywhere shared.

Measured on PG17 with 52k eval sets as a non-admin (before -> after):
eval-set list 16.2 s -> 97 ms, samples page 14.5 s -> ~0.2 s, jobs (all)
29.8 s -> 1.27 s, scans 5.8 s -> 150 ms, analyst count(*) eval 18.5 s -> 1.2 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The relay now requires the API's /monitoring/jobs/{id}/access route, but it

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: remove code-access leftovers nothing calls

The list checks became set-based, so these have no callers left:
- SQL helpers code_groups_have_access, code_groups_for_role,

  grants and health-check entries
- CodePolicyUnavailableError and PermissionChecker's raise_on_unavailable
- permissions' second copy of the code-group name regex

Transcript-only scans now check their sources with one
code_denied_eval_set_ids call, not one query per 500 eval sets.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: run per-row code checks in PL/pgSQL

Search checks code access once per hit, and RLS once per row a reader
reads. As SQL functions, every call set up all of the decision's
subqueries, including the scan-source query on eval rows that never run
it. PL/pgSQL keeps only grantable claims once, looks the policy up once
and runs the source query only for scans; the RLS wrapper, the strict
check and the read check share that tail. Scan checks also stop looking
up observed sources a second time when they are already declared.

Same seed (52k eval sets), non-admin:
- 1000 search hits: 53 -> 21 ms (model check alone: 1.3 ms)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: report code policy lookup failures to Sentry

A failed lookup denies access, and was logged at warning, below Sentry's
default event level. A database outage in the API, S3 reader or token
broker looked like ordinary denials.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: cover the read check's row groups and empty-subject guard

Mutation checks found two guards no test exercised: the read check's
required row groups, and the owner waiver's refusal of an empty subject
(no test job had an empty created_by).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(db): hold a late link's source policies until it commits

Linking a scan result refreshes the scan's code_groups from its source eval
set's policy without locking that policy. A concurrent change to the source
policy could not see the uncommitted link, skipped the scan, and the scan kept
the source's old groups after both committed. Lock the linked samples and
their eval-set policies first, as the scan writer already does
(lock_scan_sources): the change then waits and refreshes the scan. NOWAIT,
because this is out of lock order; every caller retries lock conflicts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: check code access against each run's code_groups copy

Model checks compare the model_groups each row carries. Code checks instead
re-derived every decision from the live code_policy row, which cost 1.7-3.4x
the model check on lists and 4-7x on direct SQL. Each eval, job and scan row
already carries its policy's code_groups, rewritten in the same transaction
as every policy change, and a missing, incomplete or pending policy carries
__unresolved__. Compare that copy instead, as model checks do:

- RLS compares the row's copy inline; the per-row wrapper is gone.
- Listings and per-run checks read the copy, and the owner waiver runs only
  when the copy denies. They are PL/pgSQL with generic plans: a SQL function
  is planned on every call, and a custom plan inspected each of 52k candidates.
- Search and the evals page compare eval rows' copies inline.
- Deleting a policy unresolves its rows and dependent scans, truncating or
  moving one is refused, and every policy keeps a positive revision: the
  states only the live check covered.

Same seed (52k eval sets), code check vs model check: eval-set list 25 vs
13 ms, jobs 48 vs 97 ms, scans 2 vs 18 ms, one eval set 0.2 vs 0.3 ms.
Direct SQL count(*) gains 0-10 ms on eval, job and scan (was 184-569 ms).

Before enforcing, rederive non-legacy policies so the copies are current.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The eval-set, jobs and samples listings already read the eval or job rows
that carry their runs' code_groups copies, so compare the copy there, as

Same seed, main vs this branch: eval-set list 69 vs 70 ms, jobs (all)

Under code enforcement a scan's source eval set needs a code policy; like

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The late-result linker found its samples three times: to lock them, to lock

Listings checked "copy fits, or the owner waiver allows" per row, so the

A run launched without an eval_set_id saves its config without one, and a

the saved config's missing ID from the route before comparing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The relay's access route checked the warehouse model groups with read grants.

could attach to a run whose warehouse groups gained `x`. Relay sessions can

* test(api): restore the final launch code recheck test

* fix: don't block scan writers on results awaiting their samples

A scanner result whose sample isn't imported yet adds __unresolved__ to its
scan's code groups, which hides the scan from readers until the result links.
Launch, resume and import used the readers' check, so such a scan, and an
online-scanning eval set, could not be resumed by anyone, admins included,
until the import finished; a stuck import blocked it for good.

Writers now use `code_policy_has_write_access`: the readers' check, except

The admin read bypass skipped code checks entirely, so a Hawk admin (the

(HWK-84, design v3 §8) gives admins no content visibility beyond their
groups, and model checks have no admin bypass. Admins now pass only
`__unresolved__` (missing, incomplete or pending inventories), which keeps
the repair case, and need named code groups like anyone else. Usage
telemetry, which the spec lets admins see, is unchanged.

The token broker checked each scan source against the caller's code groups
only. A caller holding code-access-x could launch a code-public scan, have

write results derived from it into a folder S3 readers reach under the
scan's weaker groups until the import catches up. Model access already
requires source models to fit the scan's output policy; code now matches:

* docs(hawk): describe the code write rule and broker source coverage

The data-function grant loop picked writers with has_table_privilege, which

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The code check was a restrictive policy on eval, job and scan. Restrictive
policies apply to every role, so the API (an rls_bypass member) kept a
filter that PostgreSQL can't simplify away, and it could no longer use

samples model filter 14 -> 119 ms and rare-term search 1.7 -> 60 ms.

everyone else it's model AND code, as before. Services keep the same
explicit pass. The same rows come back for reader, code-group, public-only

now fail if another permissive policy sits beside the model policy, or if a

concurrent ANALYZE). Locking the tables first breaks the cycle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): answer 503, not 403, when the code policy can't be read

Permission-checker reads turned an unreadable code policy into a denial,
so a database outage read as missing permission, unlike the relay, token
broker and S3 reader. Raise a 503 instead (no configured database still
denies), and answer it from the scan-view middleware, where a raised
exception would become a 500.

Also correct docs a review found stale: the S3 reader's 404 vs 503 and
its Identity Center lookup, non-admin reads after interrupted
preparation, approvals among the writers, the write rule's unlinked
results, and a 503 from the relay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(core): decide admin reads without a policy from the run's rows

The admin read path allowed any run with no code_policy row, assuming it
had no named groups. Legacy scans without a job ID never get a policy
and keep their named groups on the row, so an admin who couldn't list
such a scan could still open it. Fall back to the run's row copies, as
listings do, and refuse a run with no rows at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(core): let admin reads fall back to job rows too

A run with only a job row, as job listings show it, has no eval or scan copies, so the admin read refused it while the listing showed it. Decide from the job row's copy too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(api): ask the owner waiver once per eval set in the listing

bool_and over code_readable called code_policy_has_read_access for every unresolved eval. code_readable_group asks once per set, in HAVING, and only when some copy doesn't fit. Every eval of a set carries the same copy, so a search can't change the answer. At 52k sets, with 123 unresolved sets of 20 evals: 2,460 calls to 123, 142 ms to 75 ms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(db): lock the busiest tables last and audit copies before enforcing

The RLS policy statements took ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on eval, job and scan first and held it while later statements waited on code_policy, on every retry. Install them after the copy guard and before the scan trigger toggle, so its lock isn't upgraded, and restore them last on downgrade. The migration also refuses to apply while a copy is looser than its policy or an eval set's copies differ: runbook step 3, now enforced.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(db): keep named groups on unresolved rows when a policy is deleted

The delete trigger replaced every copy with the sentinel, dropping the named groups admins still need. Skip rows that already carry it; the stamp triggers would undo an append. A complete policy deleted by hand still loses them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(relay): require api_url when kubeconfig is set

Without it every attach failed as a 403; now it's a startup error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: say when admins pass missing policies and how to fix split copies

A run with no policy is decided from its rows' copies and refused when Hawk has none. Runbook step 3 now counts a stricter copy that splits its eval set, and names the fix. The usage-label comment names the one policy-less job row that can keep named groups.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): keep the 503 when sample-edit checks can't read the code policy

The permission checks run in a task group, which wrapped the 503 in an ExceptionGroup; the app handler unwraps only ClientError groups, so sample edits and both append-event routes answered 500. Re-raise the HTTPException from the group, as scan and eval-set creation do. Denials still reach the handler as a ClientError group (403).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(token-broker): check the sources' code access in /validate

/validate runs before authorize(), so a source the caller can't read passed pre-flight and was refused later with a code-specific 403. Ask the same sources-only check the credential request makes (no source_of: the scan has no policy yet) and answer like a model denial, or 503 when the policy can't be read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(db): run the copy audit once, not on every lock retry

Its own lock_retry call keeps the 2 s lock timeout (env.py sets no statement timeout), but _install's retries no longer repeat its three scans and GROUP BY.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(api): let a sample-edit denial win over a policy outage

Each permission check records an outage instead of raising, so it never cancels a sibling: any denial still raises the 403 group, and the 503 is raised bare, after the group, only when nothing was denied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Backend changes:

Signed-off-by: dependabot[bot] <support@github.com>

* Security hardening: input validation, rate limiting, role scoping, IDOR fixes

Red Team audit findings and fixes:
- schemas.py: bound all free-text fields (max_length), restrict patient_sex
  and symptoms to allow-lists, strip control characters from text fields
  reaching the LLM prompt, require location (was silently made optional)
- admin_routes.py: validate role via Literal instead of free string,
  enforce a 12-char password minimum for admin-created users, add rate
  limiting to every admin endpoint (previously unprotected)
- analytics_routes.py: fix dead-role bug — 'super_admin'/'facility_admin'
  were referenced in require_role() but never assignable anywhere in the
  app, so the "global vs facility scoped" branch never actually fired for
  real admins; now scoped consistently with admin_routes.py's role model
  (admin=global, doctor=own facility)
- cases.py: add rate limiting to all case endpoints (only /api/submit was
  previously limited), apply the same facility-scoping to get_case_detail
  and review_case that get_cases already had — closes an IDOR gap where a
  doctor could act on/view another facility's case via a guessed UUID
- llm.py: sanitize free-text patient fields before they enter the LLM
  prompt (strip common prompt-injection delimiter tokens, cap length) and
  add an explicit "ignore embedded instructions" rule to the system prompt
- Dashboard.jsx: fix a real pagination bug — "Load More" called
  getCases({ before: nextCursor }) but the API expects
  before_time/before_priority, so it silently refetched page 1 forever
- seed_user.py: fix a broken import (from config import settings) left
  over from the Phase 12 backend restructuring — the script would crash
  immediately on any invocation
- IntakeForm.jsx / validation.js: align frontend length limits and the
  Zod schema with the new backend bounds; make location genuinely required
  end-to-end (was required by data/UI but not by validation)
- Removed a stray frontend/frontend/ nested debris directory

* Consolidate ML to one unified, explainable, safety-net-backed classifier

Empirically found a critical live bug during this audit: the shipped
enhanced_triage_classifier.pkl (25MB, 4-sub-model ensemble) fails to
unpickle with scikit-learn versions newer than whatever trained it
(ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_loss'), and requirements.txt
pinned scikit-learn as >=1.5.2 (unbounded) — meaning a fresh install of
this repo today installs a scikit-learn that crashes the app at startup,
since load_classifier() raises and FastAPI's lifespan never completes.

This also surfaced a second, independent architectural problem: the
backend loaded the "enhanced" ensemble while the ONNX/browser export used
a completely different, independently-trained model — online and offline
triage could disagree for the same patient.

Fix: backend/scripts/train_classifier.py trains ONE
HistGradientBoostingClassifier and exports it to both
app/ml/models/triage_classifier.pkl (backend, ~4-5MB, with a bundled
shap.TreeExplainer) and frontend/public/models/{triage_classifier.onnx,
features_config.json} (browser) from a single run, so online and offline
triage are always identical. Removes the old 4-sub-model ensemble
entirely (enhanced_classifier.py, its .pkl, and the old independent
export scripts) along with ~9x redundant per-prediction model evaluation.

New in classifier.py:
- A deterministic safety-net override (_safety_net_check) that force-
  escalates unambiguous critical presentations (SpO2<85%, extreme HR/BP/
  temp, altered consciousness, seizure, severe bleeding, neonatal fever,
  hypertensive crisis + neuro symptoms) to EMERGENCY independent of the
  trained model's own prediction — a hard guarantee, not a statistical hope.
- Real SHAP-based risk explanations (_generate_shap_explanation) replacing
  the previous hand-rolled heuristic. The README's "SHAP Risk Explanations"
  claim was previously false — the loaded ensemble never bundled a SHAP
  explainer at all; this makes it true.

Training labels are generated by an evidence-informed scorer loosely
modelled on NEWS2 aggregate scoring, qSOFA, and paediatric (APLS/PALS)
vital-sign reference ranges, decoupled from data generation to avoid the
model learning generation-bucket artifacts — full clinical rationale and
limitations documented in backend/app/ml/README.md (new).

Test-set performance: ~99.4% accuracy, ~99.3% EMERGENCY recall on 5,400
held-out samples (36,000 total, class-balanced). requirements.txt now
pins scikit-learn to an exact version with a comment explaining why.

Also fixes frontend/src/utils/triageClassifier.js to fetch feature order
from features_config.json at load time instead of a hard-coded array —
this was planned in IMPROVEMENTS.md but never actually implemented; it
closes the last silent-drift risk between the Python feature engineering
and its JS port.

* Cut initial bundle size via role-based lazy loading (weak-hardware target)

App.jsx statically imported ASHAPanel, DoctorPanel, and AdminPanel — every
user downloaded and parsed all three role panels even though a given
account only ever renders one of them. Converted to React.lazy() +
Suspense so each user only fetches their own role's panel.

Combined with the onnxruntime-web changes already landed (WASM-only
'/wasm' subpath instead of the default WebGPU-inclusive entry: ~25MB ->
~12MB; dynamic import instead of a static top-level import so the ~70KB
ort JS glue isn't in the main chunk for users who never trigger offline
inference), the initial JS bundle for a typical user dropped from 908KB
to roughly 400-480KB depending on role (measured via `npm run build`),
which matters directly for the stated goal of running acceptably on
decade-old, low-RAM hardware over slow rural connections.

* Rewrite docs to match reality; add CODEBASE_MAP.md and FEATURES_ROADMAP.md

README.md was significantly stale: it documented a SQLite DATABASE_URL
that has never existed in this codebase (VitalNet is Supabase-only),
omitted every required Supabase env var, referenced `uvicorn main:app`
(pre-Phase-12-restructuring path, now `app.main:app`), and made no
mention of the offline-first PWA capability that is most of the product.
Rewrote it to accurately describe setup, env vars, architecture, testing,
deployment, and security posture.

AGENTS.md fixes: a hardcoded stale absolute path from a different
machine/environment, wrong `python test_direct.py` invocation (file moved
to tests/ in Phase 12), wrong `from database import ...` import example,
and ML constraints text that didn't reflect the now-exact scikit-learn pin
or point at the current training script.

Added a short [!NOTE] superseded-by-CODEBASE_MAP.md banner to the three
historical phase-execution logs (ARCHITECTURE_RESTRUCTURE.md,
IMPROVEMENTS.md, REBUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md) so a future reader doesn't
mistake "what we planned to do in March 2026" for "what the code does
today" — several of their file paths predate the Phase 12 package
restructuring and no longer exist.

New: CODEBASE_MAP.md — a living, file-by-file map of the repository
(backend package structure, frontend directory structure, the core
request/data flows, the auth/role-scoping model, and an explicit "what
not to change without strong reason" list) meant to be updated in the same
commit as any structural change, so a future contributor doesn't need a
full codebase re-read to orient.

New: FEATURES_ROADMAP.md — a tiered, reasoned feature backlog (why each
feature matters specifically for VitalNet's rural offline-first context,
not generically) with implementation-ready specs: schema changes, new
endpoints, frontend integration points, and explicit tradeoffs/open
questions for the larger items. Tier 1 includes closing the
version-controlled-migrations gap this audit found (RLS policies
currently exist only in the live Supabase project, not in this repo).

backend/.env.example: added the previously-undocumented but supported
GEMINI_API_KEY and FRONTEND_URL settings from app/core/config.py.

* Round 2 security: hybrid JWT auth, is_active enforcement, headers, IDOR/PII fixes

Auth (app/core/auth.py) — was doing a Supabase network round-trip on EVERY
authenticated request, and the loaded supabase_jwt_secret was never used.
Now verifies the JWT signature/exp/aud LOCALLY (HS256) on the hot path with a
network get_user() fallback for asymmetric-key projects, removing a
Supabase dependency from every request (big latency win + resilient to
Supabase-auth outages). Also adds a short-TTL is_active/revocation re-check:
the backend previously NEVER checked profiles.is_active, so a deactivated
user's unexpired token still worked — now they're cut off within
revocation_recheck_seconds (default 300s) instead of the full ~1h token TTL.

cases.py — the rate-limit key now uses the signature-VERIFIED sub
(verify_sub_for_rate_limit), so an attacker can't forge a token carrying a
victim's sub to burn the victim's budget; and the limiter storage is
configurable (RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_URI) for shared multi-instance deployments.

main.py — adds a security-headers middleware (X-Content-Type-Options,
X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control: no-store, opt-in HSTS),
tightens CORS to explicit methods/headers, and scrubs the 'input' field from
logged/returned Pydantic validation errors — that field carried patient PII
(names, vitals) straight into logs.

database.py — corrected the service-role docstring (it claimed the admin
client is never used for table data, but admin_routes legitimately uses it for
cross-tenant profiles/facilities/case_records reads) and documented that
require_role('admin') is therefore the ONLY access-control boundary on those
RLS-bypassing endpoints. Removed the dead, unused get_db_session().

seed_user.py / test_credentials.md — added explicit warnings that these are
throwaway test credentials that must never touch a production project.

* Round 2 ML: NEWS2 floor, abstention, broader training, tree-JSON export, model card

classifier.py — two clinical-safety additions on top of the existing extreme-
vital safety net:
  - NEWS2 concerning-vital floor (_news2_concerning_vital): a concerning single
    vital (NEWS2 single-parameter score >= 2, e.g. SpO2 <= 92, HR >= 120) can
    never be left as ROUTINE — it floors to URGENT. Closes the gap between
    "extreme" (safety net -> EMERGENCY) and "concerning" where the model could
    previously under-triage.
  - low_confidence abstention flag (top proba < 0.55 or top-two margin < 0.15),
    surfaced in the intake UI as "model uncertain — clinician review".
  - feature engineer is now a module-level singleton (was re-instantiated per
    prediction).

train_classifier.py — broader, more clinically realistic synthetic training:
simulates MISSING vitals (the rural no-BP-cuff / no-pulse-ox reality; scorers
made None-safe) and edge syndromes (silent MI / atypical presentation,
sepsis-without-fever). Adds 5-fold stratified cross-validation and Expected
Calibration Error reporting (ECE 0.0016 — probabilities already well-calibrated,
so no parity-breaking calibration transform is applied).

scripts/tree_export.py (new) — extracts the trained tree ensemble from the
in-memory ONNX model into compact triage_trees.json for pure-JS offline
evaluation, plus a Python reference evaluator. Training now asserts
pkl == onnx == tree-JSON on 2000 held-out samples and emits golden vectors for
the frontend JS parity test. The shipped .onnx is removed (no longer loaded).

MODEL_CARD.md (new) — intended use, full metrics with an explicit statement of
what they do and don't mean (synthetic labels, not real-outcome validated),
limitations, and ethics. Held-out: 98.9% acc, 98.3% EMERGENCY recall (model
alone); CV: 99.2% acc.

* Round 2 offline engine: pure-JS tree evaluator, drop onnxruntime-web (~12 MB)

Replaces the onnxruntime-web WASM runtime entirely for offline triage. The
model is a gradient-boosted tree ensemble — it evaluates in a few thousand float
comparisons, for which shipping a general ~12 MB WASM inference engine (that
must be precached and WASM-compiled on cold start) is pure overhead on the
2 GB-class Android tablets and metered rural links this app targets.

New:
  - treeEvaluator.js — ~120-line dependency-free evaluator, a 1:1 port of the
    Python reference in scripts/tree_export.py.
  - clinicalRules.js — safetyNetCheck + news2ConcerningVital, exact JS mirrors
    of the deterministic layers in classifier.py.
  - triageClassifier.js — rewritten to the layered design (safety net -> tree
    eval -> NEWS2 floor -> low_confidence), with a rules-only fallback if the
    tree JSON can't load so triage NEVER fails, even for untrained inputs.
  - treeParity.test.mjs (npm run test:parity) — asserts the JS evaluator matches
    the server model on all committed golden vectors.

Removed onnxruntime-web from package.json. vite.config.js no longer precaches a
WASM binary; instead it precaches the ~1 MB triage_trees.json (raised the
workbox file-size cap) so offline triage is available instantly rather than a
12 MB on-demand fetch that could fail exactly when connectivity drops. Result:
production build ships ZERO WASM/ONNX; typical initial JS bundle ~380 KB.
IntakeForm surfaces the new low_confidence flag to the ASHA worker.

* Round 2 tests + CI: classifier safety properties, admin-authz guard, JS parity

New backend tests (run in CI):
  - test_classifier_safety.py — property tests for the guarantees that must hold
    regardless of learned weights: extreme vitals ALWAYS EMERGENCY, critical
    symptoms ALWAYS EMERGENCY, a concerning vital is NEVER left ROUTINE, and the
    low_confidence flag is always present.
  - test_admin_authz.py — asserts every /api/admin route is guarded by
    require_role('admin'), the only access-control boundary on the RLS-bypassing
    service-role client. A future admin route added without it fails CI.
  - conftest.py — provides fallback JWT-format fake Supabase creds so unit tests
    run fully offline; real CI secrets still win.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml): adds a ruff lint gate, runs the safety/authz
tests (excluding the live-server integration test_e2e), and runs the JS/server
parity test (npm run test:parity) so offline-vs-online divergence blocks merges.

* Round 2 docs: sync for pure-JS offline engine, hybrid auth; expand roadmap

Updated README, AGENTS, CODEBASE_MAP, and FEATURES_ROADMAP to match the round-2
code: offline triage is now pure-JS (no onnxruntime), auth is hybrid local-
verify + is_active re-check, the classifier has three deterministic layers, and
the new tests/CI gates. CODEBASE_MAP's "what not to change" list and auth/role-
scoping sections now reflect the closed IDOR and the admin-authz invariant.

Expanded FEATURES_ROADMAP with round-2 feature specs (specs only, not built):
doctor triage-override + reason capture (unlocks real-label collection for the
outcome-retraining loop), unreviewed-EMERGENCY deterioration re-alert, case
CSV/PDF export, bulk ASHA onboarding, and per-case model-version/low-confidence
provenance — each with schema, endpoint, and frontend integration detail.

* Reconcile audit branch with dev's independent security/reliability work

dev diverged from the same base with an independent Blue Team pass (14
commits) that overlaps and conflicts with this branch's round-1/round-2
work, most critically by keeping the EnhancedTriageClassifier ensemble
architecture already proven to crash on load. Per explicit direction, this
branch's architecture wins on conflicts (unified ML model, hybrid auth,
pure-JS offline engine, security fixes); dev's non-conflicting unique work
is re-applied on top so nothing valuable is lost.

Brought in from dev (adapted to this branch's 3-role model and architecture):
- Auth: profiles.role/facility_id now resolved fresh per request (short-TTL
  cached, same mechanism as is_active) instead of trusted from stale JWT
  user_metadata; fixes a fail-open bug on a missing profile row.
- main.py: GZip compression, CSRF+X-Device-Id guard, additional security
  headers, correlation-ID middleware, docs gating, DB schema-compatibility
  startup gate, role-gated /api/health with proper 503 on degraded.
- Version-controlled Supabase migrations (backend/supabase/migrations/):
  schema constraints, indexes, case_reviews + phi_audit_log tables, RLS
